entries.title: Exponential functionals of two random walks and stationary measures of discrete growth processes
entries.abstract: We study random walks with geometric or log-gamma increments, reweighted by certain exponential functionals. We establish precise asymptotics for all moments of exponential functionals, revealing a phase transition as the drifts of the walks vary. To describe the large time limit of reweighted random walks, we introduce a discrete $T$ transformation on random walk paths and establish Girsanov relations. As a corollary, we show that the stationary measures of geometric last passage percolation and the log-gamma polymer on a strip converge to their half-space counterparts as the strip width tends to infinity. In the log-gamma case, this provides an alternative proof of a recent result in arXiv:2607.17030.

entries.title: Scaling Limits of Density Fluctuation Fields of the Symmetric Partial Exclusion Processes Approaching the Zero Range Process
entries.abstract: We study equilibrium fluctuations for the symmetric partial exclusion process (SPEP) on the one-dimensional integer lattice $\mathbb{Z}$, an interacting particle system in which each site is occupied by at most $α$ particles. We assume that the jump rate is decomposable and that the instantaneous current admits a gradient form. Our aim is to study the scaling limit of the density fluctuation field of the SPEP starting from an invariant measure and to derive the corresponding stochastic partial differential equation (SPDE). A distinctive feature of our setting is that the maximum number of particles per site depends on the scaling parameter $n$ as $α=α_n \propto n^a$ for some $a>0$, so that the model interpolates between the partial exclusion process ($α<\infty$) and the symmetric zero range process (SZRP, $α= \infty$). Under the diffusive rescaling in which the lattice spacing is $1/n$ and time is accelerated by a factor $n^2$, we prove that the density fluctuation field converges to the solution of the stochastic heat equation. The limiting SPDE coincides with the one obtained for the SZRP. A key ingredient in the proof is the convergence, under a suitable rescaling, of the partition function of the reversible measure of the SPEP to that of the SZRP. This convergence implies that expectations of a wide class of local functions under the reversible measure of the SPEP converge to the corresponding expectations under the reversible measure of the SZRP, and provides a rigorous sense in which the SPEP approximates the SZRP as $n\to\infty$.

entries.title: Percolative MDLA: phase transition and critical behaviour
entries.abstract: In this paper we introduce the model of Percolative MDLA (PMDLA) on $\mathbb{Z}^2$ which engulfs the entire occupied percolation component of each particle that reaches the aggregate. We prove a phase transition of finite time explosion, as a function of the particle density $λ$, where the critical value equals $λ_c=-\log(1-p_c^{\rm site}(\mathbb{Z}^2))$. Below $λ_c$, the process is nonexplosive and has a linear upper bound on its radius. For $2/3<λ<λ_c$, it also has a linear lower bound on the growth rate. Above $λ_c$, an infinite component is swallowed in finite time a.s. At $λ_c$, every update is finite, but the updates accumulate in finite time, causing a blowup. Excluding criticality, the results are generalized to all higher dimensions.

entries.title: Superdiffusive Invariance Principle for the two-dimensional Asymmetric Simple Exclusion Process
entries.abstract: We consider the Asymmetric Simple Exclusion Process (ASEP) at its critical dimension $d=2$, started from the Bernoulli product measure with density $ρ\in (0,1)$. We first derive the sharp $\log(t)^{2/3}$ divergence of the bulk diffusivity, predicted via mode-coupling theory in [H. van Beijeren, R. Kutner, H. Spohn, Phys. Rev. Lett., 1985], including the exact prefactor, thereby removing the subleading diverging multiplicative corrections in the Tauberian bounds of [H.-T. Yau, Ann. of Math., 2004]. More importantly, we establish an invariance principle for the density fluctuation field on the corresponding superdiffusive scales. On the time scale $τ$, we rescale space by $\sqrtτ \log(τ)^{1/3}$ in the direction of the drift and by $\sqrtτ$ in the transverse direction, and prove functional convergence of the rescaled fluctuation process to the solution of a conservative stochastic heat equation with additive noise. This is the same explicit Gaussian Fixed Point obtained in [G. Cannizzaro, Q. Moulard, F. Toninelli, arXiv:2501.00344, 2025] for the two-dimensional Stochastic Burgers Equation (SBE). We also deduce a superdiffusive central limit theorem for the second-class particle under the same anisotropic rescaling. The result holds for any finite-range jump kernel with nonzero drift and uniaxial asymmetry. This is the first space-time scaling limit result for a nonequilibrium interacting particle system at the critical dimension, where Gaussian fluctuations emerge despite logarithmic corrections to the scaling. The proof uses an approximate fluctuation-dissipation relation, which is obtained by combining a sharp quantitative comparison between the ASEP and SBE generators with refined estimates on the SBE Ansatz. An additional key novelty is a tightness argument that overcomes the limitations of the Itô trick on superdiffusive scales.

entries.title: Maximum degree for random geometric graphs in the connectivity regime and beyond
entries.abstract: A random geometric graph is a random graph model whose vertex set is a binomial point process, where two vertices are connected by an edge if each lies within the ball of radius $r$ centered at the other. In this paper, we investigate the asymptotic fluctuations of the threshold radius required for the maximum degree of the graph to reach a target value. Assuming this target value grows with the number of vertices $n$ at an order of at least $\log n$ but strictly less than $(\log n)^d$, we show that these fluctuations follow a Gumbel distribution. We also investigate the spatial configurations of vertices with extremely large degrees, and show that the point process marked by their degrees converges in distribution to a Poisson point process.

entries.title: Optimal detection of geometry in random graphs and kernel matrices at critical thresholds
entries.abstract: Detection of geometry in random graphs and matrices has been extensively studied in recent years. For testing a dense random geometric graph on $n$ vertices with latent points in dimension $d$ against an Erdős--Rényi graph, the detection threshold $d\asymp n^3$ is well known since Bubeck, Ding, Eldan, and Rácz (2016). We sharpen this result by establishing the optimal asymptotic testing error in the critical regime $d/n^3\toλ\in(0,\infty)$. The log-likelihood ratio is shown to be asymptotically normal and dominated by the signed triangle count. Moreover, we consider testing the rank statistics of inner products between latent points against uniformly random ranks. We show that ranks preserve all asymptotic testing information available in the full matrix models, and a cubic statistic based on rank statistics attains the optimal asymptotic error. This then yields an asymptotically optimal test for random kernel matrices with a possibly unknown, strictly monotone kernel. The proofs combine the classical framework of Davies (1985) and Le Cam and Yang (1988) for asymptotic normality under information loss with conditional limit theorems for the models in consideration.

entries.title: Last-Coverage Probabilities of Random Walks on Cycle Graphs for Symmetric, Biased, and Time-Dependent Walks
entries.abstract: This paper studies the last-coverage vertex of a nearest-neighbour random walk on a cycle: the vertex most likely to be the final one discovered. We show that the visited vertices always form a single contiguous arc of the ring, a property we call the Connected Arc Property. This lets the walk be replaced by a two-state time-inhomogeneous Markov chain, which we call the interval-expansion representation, in which each expansion step has a probability given by the classical gambler's ruin formula. Within this framework we prove that the last-coverage probability of node k in an n-node cycle is (1-r)r^(n-1-k)/(1-r^(n-1)), where r = (1-p)/p and p is the clockwise transition probability. As p approaches 1/2, we recover the uniform distribution, giving an independent derivation of a classical result. For a walk with a deterministic time-varying bias, we give an exact series representation for the last-coverage probabilities, together with a finite truncation that serves as a computable, error-bounded approximation. All results are validated by Monte Carlo simulation, and we run experiments on sinusoidal time-varying bias. Finally, we compare generalized Petersen graphs with Erdos-Renyi graphs of matching size, finding that structural symmetry is associated with more uniform last-coverage distributions.

entries.title: Detecting Random Geometric Graphs with General Kernel
entries.abstract: We study testing a random geometric graph with a fixed kernel against an Erdős-Rényi graph with the same edge density. Under the null hypothesis, the graph has $n$ vertices and independent edges with probability $p$. Under the alternative hypothesis, latent points $X_1,\ldots,X_n$ are independent and uniform on $\mathbb{S}^{d-1}$, and edges are conditionally independent with probabilities $K(\langle X_i,X_j\rangle)$, where $p=\mathbb{E}[K(\langle X_1,X_2\rangle)]$. The goal is to determine a critical dimension $d_\star = d_\star(n,K)$: the total variation distance between the two graph laws tends to one for $d\ll d_\star$ and to zero for $d\gg d_\star$. For dense graphs, [BDER16] established $d_\star\asymp n^3$ for hard threshold kernels, whereas [MWX26] proved $d_\star\asymp n^{3/4}$ for smooth kernels with $K'(0)\ne0$. We connect these results by characterizing the detection thresholds for kernels that need not be differentiable at zero. We also determine the thresholds for smooth kernels whose first nonzero derivative at zero has finite order greater than one. Throughout these classes, signed triangle or quadrilateral counts attain the optimal detection threshold. For certain nondifferentiable kernels, quadrilateral counts are optimal while triangle counts are suboptimal.

entries.title: Sandpile avalanches in two dimensions are finite
entries.abstract: In the abelian sandpile model on $\mathbb{Z}^d$, a site with at least $2d$ grains topples by sending one grain to each neighbor. In a box $[-N,N]^d$ whose boundary absorbs grains, adding grains at random sites and toppling defines a Markov chain. Athreya and Járai (2004) constructed the stationary state on $\mathbb{Z}^d$ as the limit of its stationary distributions as $N\to\infty$. They asked whether, when a grain is added at the origin of a sandpile in the stationary state, the resulting avalanche of topplings is finite. Járai and Redig (2008) proved that the answer is yes for $d\geq 3$, using the transience of random walk. We prove, using a different method, that avalanches are also finite for $d=2$.

entries.title: BKT transition for $\mathsf{Sine}_β$
entries.abstract: We prove the Berezinskii-Kosterlitz-Thouless (BKT) phase transition in the large-distance behaviour of the two-point correlation function of the $\mathsf{Sine}_β$ point process for all $β>0$, confirming the first term of an asymptotic expansion predicted by Forrester.

entries.title: Supercritical sharpness for Ising double random currents
entries.abstract: We show that the percolation model induced by the double random current representation of the Ising model on $\mathbb Z^d$, with $d\geq 3$, satisfies local uniqueness of the macroscopic cluster with high probability for every $β>β_c$, uniformly in boundary conditions (i.e. sources). Such a result is sometimes called supercritical sharpness in percolation theory and yields a detailed description of the model via standard renormalisation techniques. As applications, we show the exponential decay of truncated correlations for the Ising model and exponential mixing for the FK-Ising measure, results previously obtained by Duminil-Copin, Goswami and Raoufi. However, our proof is considerably simpler, as it replaces the use of a highly technical multi-valued map principle with a simple sprinkling argument.

entries.title: Asymptotic Error Distributions for Euler-Maruyama Schemes with Additive Semimartingale Noise
entries.abstract: We establish a joint stable limit theorem for integrated discretization errors of finite-dimensional càdlàg semimartingales whose predictable characteristics are absolutely continuous in time and satisfy a pathwise integrability condition. The normalized integrated error, evaluated on the discretization grid, converges stably jointly with the discretized semimartingale in the vector-valued Skorokhod $J_1$-topology. No martingale representation property is assumed. We apply this theorem to the Euler-Maruyama scheme for stochastic differential equations with additive semimartingale noise. For a $C^1$ drift with locally Lipschitz derivative and a nonexplosive solution, the grid-point error normalized by $n$ converges stably jointly with the discretized driver. The limiting error solves a linear integral equation with an explicit inhomogeneous term involving the driver, an auxiliary Brownian motion, and independent uniform marks attached to the jumps. We also obtain the same limit under two alternative drift regularity conditions based on small-jump integrability or Lévy semigroup smoothing. For continuous drivers, the continuous-time error converges stably in the uniform topology.

entries.title: Critical oriented percolation enhanced along random supercritical horizontal lines
entries.abstract: We consider the oriented site percolation model in a random environment introduced by Kesten, Sidoravicius and Vares (2022), in which the horizontal lines of the lattice are independently declared bad or good, sites being open with a probability that depends only on the type of their line. We study the boundary case where the bad lines are critical and the good ones supercritical, so that the model is critical oriented site percolation enhanced along a random set of good lines. We prove that percolation occurs for any positive density of the good lines. An arbitrarily sparse set of arbitrarily weakly enhanced lines suffices, the density of good lines and the strength of the enhancement being decoupled. The proof adapts the renormalization scheme of Archer, Hartarsky, Kolesnik, Olesker-Taylor, Schapira and Valesin (2026). We show that the edge of the process travels at a positive speed, which yields crossing estimates for tilted boxes; during runs of bad lines, we rely on the box-crossing property of Duminil-Copin, Tassion and Teixeira (2018); and the renormalized model dominates the oriented percolation with geometric defects of Hilário, Sá, Sanchis and Teixeira (2026).

entries.title: Distribution tail of the distance to infinity in supercritical bond percolation
entries.abstract: We give an estimate for the distribution tail of the passage time between $0$ and $\infty$ in first-passage percolation on $\mathbb Z^d$, when the weight distribution is bounded and has a supercritical atom at $0$. A special case involves the number of disjoint cutsets between $0$ and $\infty$ in supercritical bond percolation. Besides, we show that the rate function for the upper-tail deviations of the point-to-point passage time is asymptotically polynomial near $0$.

entries.title: The Brownian bubble tea
entries.abstract: We use Loewner-Kufarev evolution to decompose the Brownian loop soup into a Poisson point process on Brownian bubbles which we call the Brownian bubble tea driven by $ρ$, where $ρ$ is the driving measure for the Loewner chain. The only assumption on $ρ$ is that the evolving boundaries are locally connected. This generalizes a similar disintegration result of Lawler and Werner to essentially optimal regularity, and includes foliations with finite Loewner-Kufarev energy as well as radial and whole-plane $\mathrm{SLE}_κ$ for all $κ\geqslant 0$. As applications, we give Brownian loop interpretations of the conformal distortion formula for Loewner-Kufarev energy and the relationships between the Loewner energy, Loewner-Kufarev energy, and the Schwarzian action.

entries.title: Point Processes and Gap Statistics for Translation Surfaces
entries.abstract: We study the behavior of saddle connection directions on translation surfaces from the point process viewpoint. We define a direction point process for saddle connections of length at most $R>0$ on every translation surface. Given a general ergodic $\mathrm{SL}(2,\mathbb R)$-invariant measure $μ$ on a stratum of translation surfaces, we also define a slope point process associated with $μ$. By utilizing the dynamics and geometry of strata, we show that for almost every translation surface, the direction point processes, rescaled by $R^2$, converge in distribution to the slope point process as $R\to\infty$. Using Palm distribution theory, we prove the existence of limiting joint gap distributions and obtain new regularity results for gap distributions associated with the general $μ$. Finally, we study how these point processes and joint gap distributions behave as the genus $g$ tends to infinity. In the principal stratum, we show that the slope point processes, rescaled by $g^2$, converge in distribution to a Poisson point process. By passing to the corresponding Palm distributions, we show that the rescaled slope gaps converge jointly to independent exponential random variables, which is in stark contrast to the known non-exponential gap distributions in a fixed genus.

entries.title: Killing random motions with finite velocity
entries.abstract: In this paper, we study finite-velocity random motions subject to a killing mechanism acting at direction changes: at each change of direction, the motion is killed with a fixed probability and remains at its current position thereafter. We first consider the one-dimensional case of a standard telegraph process. We derive the exact distribution of the position at the killing time and show that it is Laplace distributed. We also characterize the law of the process conditional on survival up to a fixed time, proving that it coincides with that of a standard telegraph process driven by a thinned Poisson process with reduced switching intensity. We further derive the full time-dependent distribution of the killed process, including both its absolutely continuous and singular components. We then extend the analysis to a planar finite-velocity random motion with infinitely many possible directions. In this setting, we derive the distribution of the killed process and obtain an explicit representation of its density in terms of modified Bessel functions and a series involving Bessel polynomials.

entries.title: Sharp dimension threshold for unique FKPP steady states and BBM recurrence
entries.abstract: We consider the existence and uniqueness of positive, bounded stationary solutions of the Fisher-KPP equation with Dirichlet boundary conditions. We establish that stationary solutions are unique, and exist if and only if the generalised principal eigenvalue is strictly positive (supercriticality), in dimension at most $6$. This is sharp: we exhibit examples both of non-uniqueness and of existence at criticality in dimension $7$ or higher, including for the classical reaction $f(u)=u-u^2$. This proves a conjecture of Berestycki and Graham in the affirmative for dimension at most $6$, and in the negative for dimension at least $7$. We thereby show that branching Brownian motion cannot survive globally without surviving locally in dimension $6$ or lower, but can do so in dimension $7$ or higher, mirroring the classical transition of Brownian motion from recurrence to transience from dimension $2$ to $3$. We further show that relaxing the strong-KPP condition results in a more general sharp dimension threshold for the uniqueness/non-existence result. These results are valid without any regularity assumptions on the domain boundary. As a corollary, we show that solutions of the evolution reaction-diffusion equation are always convergent in the long run in dimension at most $6$, whilst we exhibit non-convergent solutions in dimension larger than $6$.

entries.title: Iterated Graph Systems (III): Alexander-Orbach conjecture on hierarchical lattices
entries.abstract: Can the Alexander-Orbach conjecture hold on hierarchical lattices? We construct Gromov-Hausdorff-Prokhorov scaling limits of critical percolation clusters on hierarchical lattices in the chemical metric and determine the typical spectral dimensions of the associated diffusions. These dimensions are dense in $(1,2)$; however, outside a narrow region in dimension space, we prove that the Alexander-Orbach conjecture fails on every hierarchical lattice under consideration.

entries.title: Small perturbations of the $2d$ classical Heisenberg model
entries.abstract: Polyakov predicted in 1975 ([Pol75) that the spin $O(3)$-model (or classical Heisenberg model) should have exponential decay of correlations at all positive temperatures on $\mathbb{Z}^2$. Our main result is as follows: if we replace the Euclidean scalar product \begin{align*} \langle σ_i , σ_j\rangle = σ_i^x σ_j^x + σ_i^y σ_j^y + σ_i^z σ_j^z \end{align*} by the $λ$-modified scalar product \begin{align*} \langle σ_i , σ_j\rangle_λ:= σ_i^x σ_j^x + σ_i^y σ_j^y + λσ_i^z σ_j^z \end{align*} we show that for all $λ\in(-1,1)$, the $\mathbb{S}^2$ valued spin system with Gibbs measure $\exp(β\sum_{i\sim j} \langle σ_i,σ_j\rangle_λ)$ has power-law decay of correlations if $β$ is chosen large enough. This is the first evidence that arbitrary small smooth modifications of the classical Heisenberg model produce a BKT phase in $2d$. It was proved in the 1970s and 80s that there exist arbitrary small smooth modifications of the classical Heisenberg model which produce instead an Ising phase. In these work, they considered the regime $λ>1$ while in this paper, we consider the regime $λ<1$ which cannot be analyzed via reflection positivity and chessboard estimate. The two main ingredients used in our proof are the stability of the BKT phase under percolation type disorder ([DG25]) and weak regularity type properties of the groundstates or $\mathbb{S}^2$-valued harmonic maps associated to our $λ$-energy functional. This analytic step is interesting on its own. Finally, the exponential and power-law decay regime should be separated by a curve $λ\mapsto β_c(λ)$. We prove a rigorous lower bound in the case of the $λ$-anisotropic hemisphere model $\mathbb{S}^2_+$ which matches with RG flow predictions.

entries.title: Graph Matching in Random Geometric Graphs I: Efficient Algorithms
entries.abstract: We study the recovery of the hidden vertex correspondence between two correlated dense random geometric graphs. Each graph is generated from $n$ latent unit vectors in $\mathbb R^d$; the vectors $u_i^A$ and $u_i^B$ of corresponding vertices satisfy $\langle u_i^A,u_i^B\rangle=ρ$, and the vertex labels of the second graph are permuted by an unknown permutation $π$. For every fixed correlation $ρ\in(0,1]$ and every edge density bounded away from zero and one, we give a randomized polynomial time algorithm that recovers $π$ exactly with probability tending to one whenever $d\ge(\log n)^L$, where $L$ depends only on the correlation and the density bounds. The algorithm assigns to each vertex a signature formed by counting decorated paths with a constant number of seeds. The number of such seeded templates grows exponentially with the path length, with an arbitrarily large constant base, so the resulting statistics amplify an arbitrarily small constant correlation. We control the dependencies created by the latent geometry in two ways: when $d$ is larger than $n/(\log n)^{L_0}$ for a suitable constant $L_0$, by comparing local moments with those of correlated Erdős--Rényi graphs; for smaller $d$, by spectral estimation of the latent geometry combined with a harmonic correction. We also provide low-degree evidence for a tradeoff between the correlation and the computational cost.

entries.title: A Proof of the Erdős Matching Conjecture for Large Matchings via Sharp Tail Probability for Sums of i.i.d. Nonnegative Random Variables
entries.abstract: We resolve a conjecture of Łuczak, Mieczkowska and Šileikis on the maximal tail probability of sums of independent and identically distributed nonnegative random variables. Specifically, for every integer $k\ge1$ and every $0\le x\le1/k$, we prove \[ \sup_{\mathbb E X_1\le x}\mathbb{P}(X_1+\cdots+X_k\ge1) =\max\{1-(1-x)^k,(kx)^k\}, \] where the supremum is over nonnegative i.i.d.\ random variables $X_1,\ldots,X_k$. We also characterize all maximizing distributions. Using this result, we prove the Erdős Matching Conjecture for every fixed $k\ge3$, all sufficiently large $s$, and every $n\ge k(s+1)$. More specifically, we show that in this range, the maximum number of edges in an $n$-vertex $k$-uniform hypergraph containing no $s+1$ pairwise disjoint edges is \[ \max\left\{ \binom{k(s+1)-1}{k}, \binom nk-\binom{n-s}{k} \right\}. \] Moreover, every extremal family consists either of all $k$-sets meeting a fixed $s$-set or of all $k$-sets contained in a fixed $(k(s+1)-1)$-set.

entries.title: Spectral Measure and Tail Process for Multivariate Dynamical Extremes
entries.abstract: We study the asymptotic behavior of extreme events in multivariate stationary sequences, with particular emphasis on stochastic processes generated by dynamical systems. We develop a general framework for describing the dependence structure of extremes through two complementary objects: the tail process and the spectral measure. We first extend the enriched point-process convergence of the univariate theory to the multivariate setting, proving that the decorated point process of exceedances converges to a marked Poisson cluster process whose marks retain the componentwise and temporal structure of extreme clusters. We then construct a spectral measure for stationary sequences, which assigns weight to distinct extremal profiles and characterizes the asymptotic dependence between components, and establish a de Haan-Resnick type representation. We also relate the spectral measure to the tail process, showing that its normalized profile distribution is recovered from the angular component of the tail process. Finally, we recover the classical univariate and multivariate exceedance processes as special cases. We illustrate the theory through applications to dynamical systems, using examples in which different dynamical mechanisms give rise to distinct extremal clustering patterns and cross-dependence structures. These applications demonstrate the ability of the proposed framework to capture genuinely multivariate features of extreme events and to extract information about the underlying dynamics that is not accessible through classical exceedance processes.

entries.title: The periodic Airy line ensembles
entries.abstract: In this paper we construct a one-parameter family of periodic Airy line ensembles $\mathcal{A}^{\mathrm{per},R}$ for $R>0$ as weak scaling limits of Borodin's periodic Schur processes. We establish several properties of $\mathcal{A}^{\mathrm{per},R}$, including a determinantal point process structure with an explicit correlation kernel. We also show that, after a parabolic shift and normalization, $\mathcal{A}^{\mathrm{per},R}$ satisfies, on its domain $[-R/2,R/2]$, the same Brownian Gibbs property enjoyed by the usual Airy line ensemble. A main technical contribution of the paper is a general tightness criterion for determinantal line ensembles, which extends the argument used by Johansson in [Comm. Math. Phys. 242 (2003), 277-329] to prove a functional limit theorem for the discrete polynuclear growth model.

entries.title: Uniform-in-time propagation of chaos for singular $L^k$ interaction kernels with rates
entries.abstract: Based on a semigroup approach, we prove quantitative uniform-in-time propagation of chaos for two systems of interacting particles with singular interaction kernels $K$ of type $L^k$, $k>d$, and a contractive Lipschitz confinement force field. First, we consider a system with moderate interaction, which means that the particles interact through the mollified kernel $K\ast V^N$, for some approximation of identity $V^N = N^{dα} V(N^α\cdot),\, α>0$. Assuming that $\|K\|_{L^k}$ is sufficiently small, we obtain that for any $\varepsilon>0$ the uniform-in-time rate is of order $N^{-\min\left(α,\frac12-\frac{dα}{2}-\varepsilon\right)}$, plus an exponentially small in time contribution of the initial condition. Second, for the classical, non-mollified particle system we establish uniform-in-time propagation of chaos with rate $N^{-\min\left(α,\frac12-\frac{dα}{2}-\varepsilon\right)} + \|K-K\ast V^N\|_{L^{k}}$, plus an exponentially small in time contribution of the initial condition. The method relies on the regularity properties of the solution of the associated nonlinear Fokker-Planck equation combined with estimates of the Duhamel formulation of the mollified empirical measure, together with partial Girsanov transforms for the non-mollified system of particles.

entries.title: Weighted moments and sharp convergence rates for supercritical multitype branching processes
entries.abstract: Let $Z_n^i=(Z_n^i(1),\cdots,Z_n^i(d)), n\geqslant0$, be a supercritical $d$-type branching process starting from a single particle of type $i\in\{1,\cdots,d\}$, where $d$ is a positive integer. The Kesten-Stigum theorem states that if the mean matrix $M$ of the offspring distribution has spectral radius $ρ>1$ with the associated positive left and right eigenvectors $u$ and $v$, then for all $1\leqslant i \leqslant d$, the sequence $W_n^i=\langle Z_n^i,u\rangle/ρ^n u(i)$ forms a non-negative martingale, and hence converges almost surely to a random variable $W^i$ as $n\rightarrow\infty$. In this paper, we investigate the asymptotic properties of the martingale $\{W_n^i\}$, focusing on weighted moments and sharp rates of convergence. We establish necessary and sufficient conditions for the finiteness of $ϕ$-moments of $W^i$, where $ϕ(x)=x^α\ell(x)$ with $α\geqslant1$ and $\ell$ is a positive function slowly varying at infinity. We also determine the sharp exponential rate of convergence of $W_n^i$ to $W^i$ in the $ϕ$-moment sense, identify a phase transition at the critical rate $ρ^{1/2},$ and characterize the behavior at the critical value. Our proofs rely on the double martingale structure of the fundamental martingale and on convex inequalities for martingales.

entries.title: Fundamental Limits of Covert queueing under Busy-Period Observations
entries.abstract: Consider a queueing system operated by Bob, which is intended to serve only jobs generated by a legitimate user, Willie. Willie's jobs arrive according to a Poisson process, and the service times are exponentially distributed. Bob seeks to covertly serve additional jobs arriving according to an independent Poisson process, without Willie detecting their presence. As the legitimate user, Willie is provided with certain statistics of each busy period by Bob. In particular, we consider two statistics: (i) the number of jobs served during each busy period and (ii) the duration of each busy period. We establish that, under either statistic, the maximum expected number of additional jobs that Bob can covertly serve obeys a square-root law. Specifically, over n busy periods, Bob can covertly serve additional jobs in the order of square root of n, whereas any scaling which is above square root of n enables Willie to asymptotically detect the presence of these additional jobs with vanishing error probability. Furthermore, we characterize the scaling constant associated with the square-root law, which we refer to as the covert queueing constant, for each of the two statistics. We compare the scaling constants corresponding to the two statistics and argue that the scaling constant under statistic (i) is no greater than that under statistic (ii).

entries.title: Metastable confinement of particle systems near linearly stable McKean-Vlasov equilibria
entries.abstract: We establish a general metastability principle showing that the local stability of a McKean-Vlasov equilibrium implies exponentially long confinement of the associated particle system. Consider interacting diffusions on $\mathbb{R}^d$ with a general smooth and bounded interaction kernel and a globally Lipschitz drift that is dissipative at large distances. Assume the McKean-Vlasov equation has at least one equilibrium which is locally exponentially stable. We prove that the probability that the empirical measure leaves a sufficiently small fixed Wasserstein-1 neighborhood of the selected equilibrium before time $T$ is bounded by $C(1+T)e^{-cN}$, where $N$ is the number of particles and $C,c>0$ are independent of $N$ and $T$. Consequently, confinement holds up to times $e^{γN}$, for every $0<γ<c$, with exponentially small exit probability. The proof combines an explicit Volterra construction of the linearized Fokker-Planck semigroup, a mild representation of empirical fluctuations, and exponential maximal estimates for stochastic convolutions. Our approach does not require a gradient flow structure or reversibility of the equations.

entries.title: Stationary Ergodic Mean-field Games of Constrained Singular Controls
entries.abstract: We study a stationary ergodic mean-field game of scalar type where the representative player controls a diffusion through two-sided singular controls exerted only at the jump times of an independent Poisson process. For each mean-field parameter, we solve the novel constrained ergodic singular control problem, proving that the optimal policy is of threshold type: the diffusion is reset at Poisson arrival times to the nearest boundary point of an interval. Our explicit probabilistic derivation of the stationary distributions induced by Poissonian threshold singular controls is a key contribution of independent interest. This distribution is used to construct the mean-field fixed-point map. We prove existence and uniqueness of the stationary mean-field equilibrium by combining the stationary density with the monotonicity and continuity of the optimal thresholds in the mean-field parameter. The model provides a tractable framework for a case study of partially reversible investment with singular adjustments under exogenous intervention constraints.

entries.title: Zeros of the Spectrogram of White Noise with Hermite Windows
entries.abstract: We study the zeros of the spectrogram of complex white noise analyzed with Hermite windows of order n, extending the classical Gaussian-window correspondence with Gaussian Analytic Functions to the polyanalytic setting. Using the polyanalytic Bargmann transform, these zeros split into two families according to the sign of the local Jacobian, giving rise to a natural notion of charge, and we show that these zeros are almost surely simple, isolated, and form a translation and rotation-invariant point process. We derive closed-form expressions for the one-point intensity, decomposed by charge, and also for the unsigned, signed, and hybrid two-point intensities. Besides, we prove that unlike the total repulsion observed with a Gaussian window, the Hermite window of order n generates a pair correlation function that converges at the origin to a strictly positive constant depending on n. Finally, we propose a numerical method for detecting spectrogram zeros via the winding number around candidate local minima.

entries.title: Ancestral circulation beyond two Fleming-Viot particles
entries.abstract: Reversible motion can produce a directed circulation of surviving ancestry in a \FV\ particle system. We prove that two particles are the exact threshold for universal ancestral balance in finite systems with uniform copying. For two particles, the stationary current of surviving labels vanishes for every finite irreducible reversible Markov chain and every positive killing vector. On a fixed complete three-state graph, nonzero circulation occurs for each population size at least three on an open dense set of killing vectors of full Lebesgue measure. A single killing vector produces circulation simultaneously for every population size at least three, and such vectors form a dense $G_δ$ set of full measure. The current is divergence free and vanishes on bridges, so three sites and three particles are the smallest possible setting for circulation. We also identify the probabilistic effect of this circulation: for sufficiently rare transplants, migration followed by fixation is more likely in one direction than in the reverse direction.

entries.title: Intermittency for the parabolic Anderson model on spaces with sub-Gaussian heat kernel estimates
entries.abstract: We study the parabolic Anderson model $\partial_t u=Δu+βu\,\dot W_α$ on an unbounded Ahlfors $d_h$-regular Dirichlet metric measure space whose heat kernel satisfies two-sided sub-Gaussian estimates with walk dimension $d_w$. The noise is white in time and, in space, either white ($α=0$) or colored through the Riesz kernel of $(-Δ)^{-2α}$, where $0\le 2α<d_h/d_w<1+2α$. No recurrence is assumed. We prove existence, uniqueness and Hölder regularity of the mild Skorohod solution for bounded initial conditions. For nonzero nonnegative bounded initial conditions, the solution is positive and its moment Lyapunov exponents exist for every real $p\ge1$, independently of the spatial point and the initial condition. For $p\ge2$, these exponents have order $p\,(β^2(p-1))^{d_w/((1+2α)d_w-d_h)}$, with upper and lower bounds matching up to constants.

entries.title: Asymptotic behaviour for escaping an interval by Lévy flights under stochastic resetting
entries.abstract: The resetting of stochastic processes has become a key mechanism appearing in many research fields, such as searching for a target, the transmission control protocol, biology, chemistry, finance, insurance, etc., with the main interest concerning the first passage time (FPT) by the process under resetting. In this paper, we focus on the exit time $\mathcal{T}_L$ from the interval $(-L, L)$ of Lévy flights (LF) under resetting, but we also consider spectrally negative Lévy processes (SNLP). As the main result, we find the asymptotics of the mean first passage time (MFPT) as $L$ tends to $+ \infty$. For LF with $α\in (0, 2)$, the scaling behaves as $L^α$ regardless of the reset rate and the asymmetry of the initial condition, a behaviour completely different from that for the known case of Brownian Motion ($α=2$). For the symmetric $α$-stable case with $α\in (0, 2)$, we also found that taking $r \to \infty$ with fixed $L$ yields a finite MFPT, which therefore may be used as a valid approximation. For completely asymmetric stable processes, we show that the scaling is very different from that for LF, and point out a method to obtain the exact distribution of FPT under resetting. The analytical calculations are verified by numerical simulations of the processes under resetting.

entries.title: Gaussian rigidity and width of measures
entries.abstract: Given $0\le m<n$ and a positive Radon measure $μ$ on $\mathbb R^n$ with at most polynomial growth, assume that it has finite $m$-dimensional \emph{Gaussian discrepancy}, defined as $$\mathcal D(μ):=\limsup_{R\to\infty}\Bigl[R^2\sup_{x\in\mathrm{spt}μ}|G_R^μ(x)-1|\Bigr],$$ where $G_R^μ(x):=(4πR^2)^{-m/2}\int_{\mathbb R^n} e^{-|z-x|^2/(4R^2)}\,dμ(z)$. Provided that $μ$ admits a flat blow-down $\mathcal H^m\llcorner V$ (an assumption that cannot be dropped entirely), we prove that there exists a finite (smallest) $0\leδ<\infty$, called the \emph{width} of $μ$, such that $$\mathrm{spt}μ\subseteq \bar B_δ(V+x_0),\quad δ^2\le C(m,n)\mathcal{D}(μ),$$ where $\bar B_δ(V+x_0)$ denotes the closed $δ$-neighborhood of a suitable translate of $V$. Note that the exponent is optimal because of scale invariance. In particular, when $\mathcal D(μ)=0$, the support of $μ$ is included in an $m$-dimensional affine plane. We use this fact to give a simpler proof of Preiss's rectifiability theorem: while still based on Gaussian averages of $μ$, this new proof avoids showing uniqueness (and hence conicality) of blow-downs of $m$-uniform measures, as well as studying Gaussian-weighted moments beyond second order. The strategy of proof consists of an anisotropic blow-down of $μ$, followed by an analysis of the resulting Young measure, using a rigidity lemma involving the heat semigroup.

entries.title: Jump limits of continuous multiscale diffusions: Homogenization under heavy-tailed activity bursts
entries.abstract: We show that purely continuous microscopic diffusions can homogenize to a Markov process with genuine jumps. Consider a multiscale diffusion with time-dependent generator $\mathcal{L}_{0}+r_{t}^ε\mathcal{L}_{1}$ driven by a regenerative random environment. When the integrated activity over a regeneration cycle has a regularly varying tail of index $β\in(0,1)$, the cumulative operational clock converges to a $β$-stable subordinator, compressing finite activity-driven diffusion into vanishingly short physical time intervals. To overcome the noncommutativity of $\mathcal{L}_0$ and $\mathcal{L}_1$, we develop an extended-time parametrization paired with Khasminskii-type time discretization, establishing finite-dimensional convergence and strong semigroup convergence on $C_{0}(\mathbb{R}^{d})$ toward a jump process with nonlocal generator $\overline{\mathcal{L}}=\mathcal{L}_{0}-κ(-\mathcal{L}_{1})^β$. Under uniform ellipticity of $\mathcal{L}_{1}$, the fractional power $(-\mathcal{L}_{1})^β$ is identified as a $2β$-stable-like nonlocal operator. We also clarify physical-time path-topology obstructions and apply the framework to Poisson resetting pulses, Ornstein--Uhlenbeck diffusions, and multiscale stochastic volatility.

entries.title: Fitting Gaussian vectors in normed spaces
entries.abstract: Given a family of $N$ i.i.d. Gaussian points in a $d$-dimensional normed space, what is the probability that some linear transformation maps it to the unit sphere? The case of a Euclidean space is known as the ellipsoid fitting problem and has recently attracted major attention. We initiate a study of this fitting problem in a general normed space, both asymptotically and in a fixed dimension. We specifically focus on the space $\ell_\infty^d$, where a combinatorial reformulation allows us to show that $cd^2/\log d$ points can be fitted with high probability. We illustrate that the geometry of the normed space is reflected in the fitting problem by showing that in dimension $2$, the spaces $\ell_2^2$ and $\ell_\infty^2$ are characterized by having extremal fittability properties.

entries.title: Entropic Inequalities and Limit Theorems in Boolean Probability
entries.abstract: We study Boolean entropy and Fisher information in information inequalities and the Boolean central limit theorem. We prove a fractional Stam inequality for the Boolean Fisher information associated with arbitrary fractional partitions of subset sums, and derive an entropy power inequality for sums of Boolean independent random variables and its weighted version. We then establish a Boolean analogue of Barron's entropy convergence result along the Boolean central limit theorem: Boolean entropy converges to the entropy of the Rademacher law if and only if the initial entropy is finite. Furthermore, under a finite fourth moment, in the Boolean central limit theorem, we obtain \[ Γ(μ_n\mid\mathbf b)= \frac{m_4(μ)-1-m_3(μ)^2}{2}\frac{\log n}{n} +o\!\left(\frac{\log n}{n}\right), \] with an explicit example showing sharpness. For symmetric laws with finite fourth moment and finite Boolean Fisher information, \[ Ψ(μ_n\mid\mathbf b) =2\bigl(m_4(μ)-1\bigr)\frac{\log n}{n} +o\left(\frac{\log n}{n}\right). \] Our approach is based on the Nevanlinna representation of Cauchy transforms.

entries.title: Drift parameter estimation for interacting particle systems with singular repulsion
entries.abstract: We study the estimation of the interaction parameter in singular interacting particle systems from continuous and discrete observations over a fixed time horizon. The singularity of the interaction drift prevents the direct application of standard likelihood and contrast-based methods, which rely on regularity assumptions that fail in this setting. Our approach exploits an exact reduction of the particle dynamics to a one-dimensional stochastic differential equation for a quadratic empirical moment. By the symmetry of the interaction kernel, the singular terms cancel, yielding an explicit estimator in which the unknown parameter enters linearly. We establish consistency and asymptotic normality as the number of particles, \(N\), tends to infinity. Letting \(\varepsilon_N\) denote the microscopic noise scaling of the system, we obtain asymptotic normality at the rate \(\sqrt{N/\varepsilon_N}\) for strictly positive interaction kernels, under an additional condition on the limiting empirical information. We further extend these results to degenerate interaction kernels, achieving consistency and asymptotic normality at rate \(N\) under suitable structural assumptions and the canonical scaling \(\varepsilon_N=N^{-1}\). In both regimes, we provide conditions on the observation mesh ensuring that the statistical limits remain valid under discrete sampling, in high frequency. Finally, we illustrate the applicability of our methodology through Dyson Brownian motion, the Dyson Ornstein--Uhlenbeck process, and Wishart--Laguerre particle systems, alongside a numerical investigation of the estimators' finite-sample performance.

entries.title: KPP type reaction--diffusion equations in narrow tubes with degenerating boundary and generalized second order operators
entries.abstract: We consider a reaction--diffusion equation with Kolmogorov--Petrovskii--Piskunov (KPP) nonlinearity and Neumann boundary conditions in a narrow tube $G^{\varepsilon,δ}\subset\mathbb{R}\times\mathbb{R}^{n}$ of width of order $\varepsilon$. The tube is chosen from a family indexed by a second parameter $δ>0$, whose boundary $\partial G^δ$ is smooth for each $δ>0$ but degenerates as $δ\downarrow0$. In the iterated limit $\varepsilon\downarrow0$ followed by $δ\downarrow0$ the problem becomes a Cauchy problem on the line whose spatial operator is a generalized second order differential operator $D_{v}D_{u}$ in the sense of Feller, rather than a classical second order elliptic operator. Solutions of the limiting problem need not be differentiable in $x$, so they must be understood in a generalized sense. Using the Feynman--Kac representation, we prove that the limiting problem has a unique generalized solution. When the cross sectional volume is bounded above and below, we also prove that this solution is Hölder continuous in $t$ with exponent $1/2$, locally uniformly in $x$, whenever it is Lipschitz continuous in $x$. Under the same volume bounds, this Lipschitz condition holds when the initial function and the nonlinearity are Lipschitz continuous in $x$. Finally we prove that the solutions in the narrow tubes converge to the generalized solution uniformly on compact time intervals in the same iterated limit if the tube, the initial function, and the nonlinearity are periodic in $x$.

entries.title: Interior smoothness and zero-variance geometry for finite-maturity Heston American puts
entries.abstract: We study finite-maturity American puts in the Heston model without the Feller condition. At positive variance, the exercise boundary is smooth and strictly decreasing in remaining maturity and variance. At zero variance, the endpoint is locally Lipschitz in remaining maturity, the boundary moves with bounded speed in maturity uniformly down to zero variance, and it extends continuously to the axis. Each boundary slice at positive maturity has a regular $C^1$ closure tangent to the zero-variance axis, its stock threshold has variance derivative tending to minus infinity, and both partial derivatives of the inverse boundary graph vanish along the slice. The continuation premium at the axis contact stock is of order variance, and as a consequence smooth fit fails in the variance direction at the axis. At expiry the whole boundary, including its axis edge, converges to the strike. We give quantitative boundary gap bounds, an exact limiting weighted boundary Hessian, and vertical identities retaining the maturity term. Exact boundary gap equivalents remain open.

entries.title: Drift and joint minimal displacement for groups acting on hyperbolic spaces
entries.abstract: We obtain a uniform lower bound for the drift of random walks on hyperbolic spaces in terms of joint minimal displacement. Our main theorem applies to weakly acylindrical actions on Gromov-hyperbolic spaces and is quantitative in all relevant constants. For discrete isometry groups of Hadamard manifolds with pinched negative curvature, the required assumptions are automatically satisfied by the Margulis lemma. This yields uniform gaps at zero in drift spectra for pinched negatively curved Hadamard manifolds, hyperbolic groups, and mapping class groups acting on curve graphs.

entries.title: From Global to Tail Convergence: Dynamics of $α$-Stable Score-Based Generative Models
entries.abstract: Score-based generative models driven by $α$-stable L{é}vy processes have been proposed as an alternative to Brownian diffusion models, with empirical evidence suggesting improved sampling and better modeling of heavy-tailed data. Yet theoretical guarantees for these models remain limited. We develop a non-asymptotic convergence analysis for scale-preserving $α$-stable generative dynamics, covering both compactly supported and power-law targets. In p-Wasserstein distance, we quantify the effects of early stopping, initialization, score approximation, and time discretization, and show exponential decay of the initialization error. A comparison with Brownian dynamics reveals that global Wasserstein convergence alone does not fundamentally distinguish the two models: both initialization errors decay exponentially with the forward horizon on the common class of heavy-tailed targets. A sharp separation emerges instead in the tails. At any positive generation time, stable dynamics produces power-law tails with index $α$, whereas Brownian dynamics remains light-tailed. For a target with tail index $ν$, asymptotically correct extreme-quantile scaling is possible precisely when $α$=$ν$. These results identify tail-index matching as a principled mechanism behind the ability of stable generative models to capture extreme events.

entries.title: Gaussian approximation for the integrated intensity of counting processes: application to Hawkes processes
entries.abstract: In this paper, we establish quantitative central limit theorems for the integrated fluctuations of the intensity of a counting process. Building on the work of Coutin and using the Clark-Ocone formula, we first derive a general upper bound on the Wasserstein distance between a Gaussian random variable and the normalized integral of the centered intensity. We then apply this result to subcritical linear Hawkes processes. In this setting, we prove that the integrated fluctuations of the intensity converge in distribution to a centered Gaussian random variable, with a convergence rate governed by the tail behavior of the resolvent associated with the underlying Volterra equation.

entries.title: Local Linearization and Exact Oscillations for the Nonlinear Stochastic Heat Equation with Spatially Rough Noise
entries.abstract: Consider the one-dimensional nonlinear stochastic heat equation $$ \frac{\partial u(t,x)}{\partial t} = \frac{\partial^2 u(t,x)}{\partial x^2} + σ(u(t,x))\dot W(t,x), \qquad t>0,\ x\in\mathbb R, $$ where $\dot W$ is a Gaussian noise that is white in time and fractional in space with Hurst parameter $H\in(1/4,1/2)$. Hu et al. ({\it Ann. Probab.} {\bf 45} (2017), 4561--4616) established existence and uniqueness of the solution under the assumptions that $σ$ is differentiable, both $σ$ and $σ'$ are Lipschitz continuous, and $σ(0)=0$. Hu and Wang ({\it Ann. Inst. Henri Poincaré Probab. Stat.} {\bf 58} (2022), 379--423) subsequently removed the technical condition $σ(0)=0$ by developing the well-posedness theory in a suitable weighted space associated with the weight $λ(x)= c_H (1 + |x|^2)^{H-1}$. In this weighted framework, which allows $σ(0)\ne0$, we establish temporal and spatial local linearizations: small increments of the nonlinear solution are approximated by the corresponding increments of the solution to the additive equation, multiplied by the local coefficient $σ(u(t,x))$. The main difficulty lies in handling the nonlocal fractional-difference structure induced by the rough spatial noise. We address this difficulty using weighted heat-kernel increment estimates. These approximations yield exact Lévy-type uniform moduli of continuity in both time and space, together with Khinchin and Chung laws of the iterated logarithm.

entries.title: Weight-adapted ANOVA kernels for high-dimensional periodic approximation
entries.abstract: In this paper, we construct normalized periodic kernels from univariate functions satisfying suitable moment conditions and derive sufficient conditions for high-order convolution approximation. Two computable quasi-interpolation schemes are obtained by discretizing the convolution integral using either a full tensor grid or random samples. In each case, the analysis separates the continuous convolution error from the error introduced by discretization. The contribution of kernel energy to the error exposes the dimensional dependence of tensor-product kernels and motivates our weight-adapted ANOVA constructions. Under suitable summability conditions on the weights, we establish convolution error and kernel energy estimates that yield dimension-uniform error bounds for the resulting quasi-interpolants. Numerical experiments corroborate the theoretical convergence rates and illustrate the effect of coordinate weighting on dimensional dependence.

entries.title: Fluctuations in the Potts spin glass model at high temperature
entries.abstract: We study the fluctuations of the free energy of the Potts spin glass with $κ$ colors at high temperature. The disorder is symmetric with unit variance and finite fourth moment. For configurations with a balanced, or nearly balanced, color profile, the log-partition function satisfies a central limit theorem whenever $β^2<α_c(κ)$. Here $κα_c(κ)$ is the critical inverse temperature of the Curie-Weiss-Potts model. A comparison of color profiles transfers this limit to the unconstrained model for $β<β_{\max}(κ)$, an explicit threshold. In the same range, the magnetizations of two replicas and their overlap matrix satisfy a joint quenched central limit theorem with independent Gaussian limits. The fourth cumulant of the disorder enters the limiting mean and variance explicitly.

entries.title: Heat Kernel Estimates for Random Walks with Killing on Transient Graphs
entries.abstract: We give matching two-sided estimates for heat kernels obtained from Schrödinger operators $Δ+W$ on weighted graphs. The graphs we consider are transient and admit two-sided sub-Gaussian heat kernel estimates for the Laplacian $Δ$, and the potentials $W$ decay to zero at infinity. We offer two proofs for one of our main results: one using the Feynman-Kac formula, and one without using it. Our results apply to fractal-type graphs such as graphical Sierpinski carpets, among other examples.

entries.title: With Leverage, the Gambler is Not the One Who Gets Ruined
entries.abstract: In this note we explore the following simple question: How does the classic \emph{gambler's ruin} phenomenon change if we allow the gambler \emph{financial leverage}? We show that, with a moderate amount of leverage, it is possible for an (idealized) gambler to sustain seemingly improbable profits over a remarkably long time horizon without ever going bankrupt, \emph{even} if the gambler makes only fair bets. With a leverage ratio of $L = 10$ (less than what Lehman Brothers Holdings had from 1995--2008), the probability of multiplying one's money by $1000\times$ without going bankrupt is roughly $50\%$. More generally, given $L$-fold leverage, and given the goal of multiplying one's money by a factor of $r > 1$, the optimal gambling strategy has probability roughly $r^{-1/L}$ of success. The results in this note are designed as part of the course development for the CMU randomized algorithms course.

entries.title: Moment-optimal Gamma approximation of Bessel Process exit times
entries.abstract: We construct finite Gamma convolutions approximating the first hitting time of $1$ by a Bessel process of index $ν>-1$ started at the origin. The scale measure in the classical exponential representation of this law is obtained by squaring the positive half of a dilated modified Lommel polynomial orthogonality measure. Its Jacobi recurrence yields an $N$-factor Gamma convolution that uniquely matches the first $2N$ cumulants, the maximal number attainable in this class. From an exact Gaussian quadrature remainder we derive supergeometric convergence of the Laplace transforms on compact subsets of a common slit plane and geometric convergence of the distribution functions uniformly on the real line. The approximants have total Gamma shape $N(N+ν+1)$, and their Laplace transforms and negative moments decrease to those of the exit law.

entries.title: $L^p_μ$-Normed Spaces of Bounded Multilinear Operator
entries.abstract: We study the spaces of bounded multilinear operators $\mathcal L^i(X,Y)$ endowed with $L^p_μ$-norms, where $X,Y$ are normed spaces and $μ$ is a measure with $p$-moments. These are norms without taking a quotient, under suitable support conditions. The topology induced coincides with the strong operator and compact-open topologies on operator-norm-bounded subsets. Furthermore, we identify the completion of these spaces with spaces of Hilbert--Schmidt operators on the reproducing kernel Hilbert space (RKHS) for $p=2$; with iterated $γ$-radonifying multilinear operators on the RKHS in the Gaussian case, for general $p$.

entries.title: On the discrete Fisher information
entries.abstract: We investigate a discrete analogue of the Fisher information. By using a discrete Laplacian operator, we can construct a discrete analogue of the score function and hence of the information. This provides a natural framework for establishing several information-theoretic inequalities in the discrete setting.

entries.title: On rigidity of infinite exchangeable sequences
entries.abstract: We ask when the law of an infinite exchangeable sequence is uniquely determined by a finite-dimensional marginal. For mixtures of a probability kernel, a weak localization condition makes three coordinates determine the directing law. Completeness alone makes four coordinates sufficient. Neither order can be lowered in general. For exponential kernels with a nonnegative sufficient statistic, a Müntz-Szász support condition implies three coordinates suffice. In the scalar case, this result is sharp. We also characterize when completeness holds simultaneously for all scalar mixing laws by a weighted Müntz density condition and show that statistic support alone need not decide completeness. These methods yield sharp finite-dimensional refinements of Freedman's theorem on rotatable sequences, namely that spherical symmetry of three coordinates makes an infinite exchangeable sequence rotatable while symmetry of the first two coordinates is in general insufficient. Finally, for energy-radial densities we give a complete-monotonicity criterion for infinite extendibility and determine the exact uniqueness thresholds for $\ell_q$-norm exponential laws.

entries.title: The forward-loop-erased ants walk
entries.abstract: In this paper, we study a new variant of the ants walk: a model of reinforced random walks for the phenomenon of a colony of ants being able to find the shortest path between their nest and a source of food. In this model, the nest and the source of food are two distinguished nodes in a finite graph. The ants perform successive random walks on this graph, started at the nest and stopped when they first hit the food source; the transition probabilities of each random walk depends on the trajectories of the previous ants, through some edge-weights that represent the amount pheromones deposited on each edge. In our new variant of the model, the ant (1) forgets loops made on the way to the food as soon as they are made, and (2) comes back to the nest following this loop-erased version of its forward trajectory, and deposits pheromone on the edges it crosses by doing so (i.e. adds one to these edges' weights). We say that the ants "find the shortest path" if, almost surely as the number of ants tends to infinity, the proportion of ants that travel along a graph-geodesic path from the nest to the food tends to one and the proportion of ants that travel along the remaining edges tends to zero. We are able to prove that this new variant of the model finds the shortest path when the graph distance between the nest and the source is at most 2. The strength of our result is that there is no other assumption on the shape of the graph. We prove this result using stochastic approximation theory, the electrical network method for random walks on weighted graphs, and the theory of weighted uniform spanning trees (WUSTs). In particular, the link with WUSTs is unique to the model studied in this paper due to the way the ant erases loops on the outward journey.

entries.title: Distribution-Dependent Improvements of McDiarmid's Inequality via Rényi Divergence
entries.abstract: We investigate whether Rényi divergence can sharpen McDiarmid's inequality and its distribution-dependent refinement induced by KL divergence. Starting from Marton's transportation proof, we show that its transport inequality fails in general when KL divergence is replaced by Rényi divergence of order $0<α<1$. For sums of independent bounded random variables, however, the additivity of Rényi divergence allows us to adapt the argument and derive concentration bounds. For Bernoulli sums, these bounds strictly improve on the distribution-dependent bound induced by KL divergence over a range of deviation thresholds. We also establish a distribution-dependent refinement of Gilardoni's inequality relating total variation to Rényi divergence, providing explicit constants for our general concentration bounds.

entries.title: Branching explosion of Brownian Fleming-Viot systems
entries.abstract: We resolve the long-standing non-extinction problem for Brownian Fleming-Viot systems in bounded domains. For every fixed N >= 3, we construct a bounded connected domain in R3 in which branching explosion occurs with positive probability before every prescribed positive time, from every interior initial configuration. On this event all particles converge to one boundary point. Together with two-particle non-extinction, this gives the sharp population threshold for bounded-domain Brownian explosion. The mechanism is directed transport generated by uniform copying in a periodic absorbing environment. We compute a positive cubic current for the same two-harmonic killing profile at every N >= 3, with an explicit population coefficient and a controlled fourth-order remainder. To realize this transport by spherical absorption, we develop a marked genealogical transfer theorem that retains the Euclidean displacement inherited at each copy. Common ancestry makes the integer winding reconstructible from phase records and yields convergence of the stationary signed current. A boundary restart law with P'olya weights supplies the continuity needed to turn that current into stable escape. Diffusion coefficients adapted to a common Kelvin clock preserve the joint Brownian law and uniform donor marks while compressing escape into finite lifetime. Disjoint spherical holes in a ball accumulate only at the explosion point. The boundary is smooth elsewhere, with finite area and perimeter. Boundary area within distance r of the singularity is of order r. For three particles, the transfer theorem covers every smooth positive periodic killing rate.

entries.title: A formula for the free energy of non-convex vector spin glasses
entries.abstract: We consider vector mean-field spin glass models with independent and identically distributed spins without assuming the covariance function is convex. We identify the limit free energy as the minimum of a functional that can be written as the sum of a relative entropy and the solution of a Hamilton--Jacobi equation. The proof of this result relies on the observation that when the spin configurations of the system are constrained to have a given empirical measure, the corresponding free energy approximately satisfies a Hamilton--Jacobi equation with a uniformly bounded error.

entries.title: A Rate Transfer Method: Convergence Rates in Stochastic Gradient Descent via Stochastic Calculus
entries.abstract: We develop a rate-transfer method that converts finite-time Lyapunov estimates for an associated stochastic differential equation (SDE) into finite-time convergence bounds for stochastic gradient algorithms. Under generic moment and smoothness conditions, the convergence analysis of the stochastic gradient method reduces to a calculus argument verifying a Lyapunov generator inequality for the SDE. The method recovers established rates for classical stochastic gradient methods and provides a way to establish convergence rates for new optimization algorithms through calculus arguments applied to their associated SDEs.

entries.title: Sampling with collective variables: Relative error analysis for umbrella sampling under general conditions
entries.abstract: We consider the problem of estimating the expectation of a function (observable) with respect to a high-dimensional probability distribution, under the assumption that a low-dimensional collective variable map captures all the directions of slow mixing for the distribution. More precisely, under the assumption that the fibers of the collective variable map satisfy a log-Sobolev inequality, we establish non-asymptotic relative-error guarantees for this problem using the eigenvector method for umbrella sampling (EMUS). Our analysis applies to both log-Lipschitz observables and indicator of convex sets, and gives complexity bounds that are polynomial in regularity parameters and inverse relative accuracy, and exponential in the dimension of the collective variable space. As a relative error guarantee, our bounds apply to rare event estimation. We consider Gaussian biasing windows defined on a low-dimensional collective variable space and analyze a modified sparse matrix version of EMUS. The bounds quantify the effect of the map through mixing of the conditional distribution and fluctuation of the observable along the fibers.

entries.title: A Randomized Approximation Algorithm for Doubly Free-Boundary Macdonald Processes
entries.abstract: We construct an approximate sampler for finite doubly free-boundary Macdonald rail-yard processes with Macdonald, boundary, and edge parameters in $(0,1)$. The construction allows arbitrary finite sequences of additions and removals of horizontal or vertical strips and all four boundary types. It reverses a finite commutation--reflection history from a partition sequence whose entries are equal, with the common partition weighted by both boundaries. We derive local reconstruction kernels from the skew Cauchy, Littlewood, and branching identities. Bulk and boundary updates combine integer increments with conditional shape sampling at a prescribed size; same-sign swaps use finite conditional resampling. For $K$ reflection periods and an initial partition-size cutoff $M$, the algorithm terminates almost surely and samples the resulting approximating law exactly. We prove total variation convergence to the target process as $K,M\to\infty$ and give explicit bounds for both truncation errors, decaying geometrically in the cutoffs for fixed input parameters. Under fixed parameter bounds, we also bound the expected operation count of direct enumeration in a unit-cost model. We further construct an exact rejection sampler for the initial partition law without a size cutoff or evaluation of its normalizing constant. Using this sampler removes the size-truncation error, leaving only the error from the finite reflection history.

entries.title: Subgaussian Vector Balancing by an Ising Model
entries.abstract: We show that the guaranties of the Gram-Schmidt Walk Algorithm of Bansal, Dadush, Garg, and Lovett can be achieved by an Ising model. Given vectors $v_1, \ldots, v_n$ of norm less than 1, we give a closed form for a centrally symmetric distribution on a vector $σ\in \{\pm 1 \}^n$ so that the signed sum $\sum_j σ(j) v_j$ is $1$-subgaussian. We show that the Glauber dynamics for this model mix rapidly provided that the norms of the input vectors are bounded below 1 by an inverse-polynomial. The proofs employ the theory of Lorentzian polynomials, and we use these techniques to show fast mixing bounds for other spin systems.

entries.title: Rapid Mixing of Stereographic MCMC for Heavy-Tailed Sampling
entries.abstract: Sampling from high-dimensional, heavy-tailed distributions is a fundamental challenge in computational statistics, as many standard Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) methods mix poorly in such settings. Recently, Stereographic MCMC [Yang et al., 2024] and the Sub-Cauchy Projection Sampler [Grazzi et al., 2026] have been shown to perform successfully on such tasks. However, establishing their non-asymptotic convergence properties remains an important open problem. In this work, we fill this gap by establishing non-asymptotic upper bounds on the mixing time of the stereographic projection and sub-Cauchy projection samplers. Our results demonstrate that, under certain conditions on the target and initial distributions, the mixing time is polynomial in dimension for a broad class of distributions, including light- and heavy-tailed cases. Motivated by the theoretical analysis, we further establish a new weighted isoperimetric inequality that extends the classical version for log-concave distributions to the heavy-tailed setting with optimal dimension dependence. The proof techniques provide new insights into the geometric properties of heavy-tailed distributions that govern rapid mixing in high dimensions.

entries.title: A pedestrian's approach to Bayesian methods for inverse problems
entries.abstract: In the past two decades, the Bayesian approach to inverse problems in infinite dimensional spaces has seen significant developments in theory, Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) methods, and in applications. The Bayesian approach in finite dimension produces posterior distributions of finite dimensional random variables. In infinite dimensions, the desired objects are random fields and their laws as measures on Hilbert or Banach spaces. There are many textbooks and tutorials available that explain Bayesian methods and MCMC in finite dimensions. To enter the field of Bayesian inverse problems in infinite dimensions, a newcomer has to engage with a quite diverse and extensive literature. The purpose of this article is to provide a basic path to the subject that is easily accessible to a reader with general knowledge in probability and mathematical analysis. We start with a swift introduction to the finite dimensional case. The infinite dimensional case is introduced for Gaussian priors on Hilbert spaces and Gaussian-type likelihood functions. In this situation, mere continuity of the forward map suffices to prove that the posterior measure is well-defined. We also give some new and simple stability results. Two application examples are elaborated, one finite dimensional, one infinite dimensional.

entries.title: The Singularity Has a Distribution: Exact Timing Laws and Detection Limits for a Stochastic Intelligence Explosion
entries.abstract: Automating AI research creates a positive feedback loop between software capability and research effort. We study a stochastic realisation of this loop in which independent, positive, multiplicative improvements arrive at a rate proportional to a power of current capability. Within this model, randomness leaves the deterministic explosion threshold unchanged but replaces the blow-up date by an explicit distribution. For equal-sized improvements the explosion time is a geometrically weighted sum of independent exponentials; its $q$-series representation gives its transforms, moments and tail behaviour, including a two-term small-time asymptotic. For Lomax-distributed improvement sizes the explosion time is exactly Gamma distributed. Self-similarity implies that, with parameters known, the relative uncertainty about the remaining time does not vanish as explosion approaches. We formulate a fixed-sample test between constant and geometrically increasing idea-arrival rates. If the baseline rate and the alternative log-rate increment $\ell$ are known, the minimum sample size at error level $α$ is asymptotic to $(12z_α^2)^{1/3}\ell^{-2/3}$, where $z_α$ is the upper-$α$ standard normal quantile. Uncertainty about the growth exponent near its critical value produces a $1/t$ tail with an explicit constant, and hence an infinite conditional mean waiting time, although explosion is certain given a positive exponent. Separate extensions show that a fixed deployment delay prevents explosion in the specified delayed-feedback models, that power-law diversion of effort shifts the growth threshold, and that in a deterministic oversight race a fixed allocation share does not change the asymptotic regime, except at a critical equality of exponents. Numerical illustrations, which are not empirical forecasts, show how timing and detectability depend on the granularity of improvements.

entries.title: A Central Limit Theorem for High-Temperature SYK Model
entries.abstract: The Sachdev--Ye--Kitaev (SYK) model is a quantum many-body model of Majorana fermions with all-to-all random interactions. It has attracted wide interest in condensed matter and high-energy physics as a solvable model of non-Fermi liquids and holography. Fix an even integer $q\geq4$, and let $Z_N(β)$ be the partition function of the Gaussian $q$-body SYK model. We prove that for all sufficiently small inverse temperatures $β> 0$, there exists $ρ=ρ(β)>0$ such that \[ N^{q/2 -1}(\log Z_N(β)-\mathbb{E}[\log Z_N(β)]) \Longrightarrow \mathcal{N}(0,ρ^2). \] In addition to the mathematical results, we discuss how the proofs were developed and refined through interaction between human researchers and AI, and we describe the subsequent formalization of the main arguments in Lean 4. This work thus serves as a case study of a research workflow that integrates human insight, AI-assisted exploration, iterative proof refinement, and formal verification.

entries.title: Stability of the Markov-Krein Transform Under Classical Convolutions
entries.abstract: We prove that, for every $c>0$, the image of the generalized Markov-Krein transform on probability measures with finite logarithmic moment is closed under classical additive convolution and under the Mellin convolution. This resolves the positivity conjecture for the additive high-temperature convolution, a one-parameter interpolation between classical and free convolution arising in random matrix theory and representation theory in the regime $N\to\infty, Nβ_N/2\to c$. Our proof relies on a convolution theorem for universally prestarlike functions.

entries.title: Quantitative Convergence of Markov Equilibria for Time-Inconsistent Controlled Diffusions
entries.abstract: Time-inconsistent stochastic control admits a natural game-theoretic interpretation in which successive decision dates are represented by different selves. In the Markovian framework of Björk-Khapko-Murgoci, the corresponding continuous-time equilibrium HJB system can be motivated by discrete subgame-perfect games, but the general discrete-to-continuous passage is not automatic. We establish a quantitative convergence theorem for a smooth uniformly elliptic class in which the control may enter both drift and diffusion. Using the exact sample-and-hold transition law on each time step, we construct, near a verified continuous equilibrium branch, a unique regular discrete Markov subgame-perfect equilibrium and prove first-order convergence of the continuation objects in an anisotropic $C^{2+β}$ topology and of the equilibrium policies in $C^0$. The key stability mechanism is structural: the discrete first-order condition forces the differential feedback correction in the frozen linearization to be nilpotent, which yields mesh-uniform block estimates through a two-norm dyadic Schauder argument despite the second-order coupling caused by controlled volatility. We also formulate a conditional transfer principle for structured polynomial-growth classes, with error-space stability stated as a separate hypothesis.

entries.title: Wong--Zakai Convergence and FNO Learning for Stochastic Volterra Equations
entries.abstract: This paper studies Wong--Zakai convergence and Fourier neural operator learning for stochastic Volterra integral equations (SVIEs) describing random systems with memory. A Wong--Zakai theorem establishes convergence of pathwise solutions driven by piecewise linear approximations of Brownian motion to the corresponding SVIE solution. This convergence provides a foundation for using mirror-padded Fourier neural operators to learn the solution operator mapping initial conditions and driving noise to entire solution trajectories. Numerical experiments demonstrate competitive prediction accuracy and generalization to temporal grids finer than those used for training, while assessing the influence of padding and computational cost. As a follow-up to \citet{LKP:26}, this study extends their operator-learning framework to SVIEs through separate convergence and approximation analyses tailored to convolutional memory.

entries.title: Strong Invariance Principle for Random Dirichlet Series
entries.abstract: It is shown that the random prime Dirichlet series $ X(s)=\sum_{p\in \mathcal{P}}\frac{ξ_p}{p^{s+1/2}} $ can be almost surely approximated by a Brownian motion, where $ \{ξ_p\}_{p\ge 1} $ are independent and identically distributed random variables with zero mean and finite variance, and $ \mathcal{P} $ is the set of prime numbers. As a consequence, the functional law of the iterated logarithm, limit laws of the iterated logarithm, and Chung's law of the iterated logarithm for $ X(s) $ are obtained. It is also shown that the random Dirichlet series $ Y(s)=\sum_{k=2}^{\infty} \frac{(\log k)^α}{k^{s+1/2}} $ with $ α=-1/2 $ admits the same approximation as $ X(s) $, and a direct relationship between $ X(s) $ and $ Y(s) $ with $ α=-1/2 $ is established. The strong invariance principle for $ Y(s) $ with $ α>-1/2 $ is also obtained.

entries.title: Free energy of non-convex multi-species Ising spin glasses with external fields
