entries.abstract: We identify the limit free energy of mean-field multi-species spin glasses with +/-1 spins, allowing for the presence of external fields, and without assuming any convexity property of the covariance function of the Hamiltonian. The limit is given by an "uninverted" variational formula over Brownian martingales. The proof consists in first identifying the limit free energy of configurations with a fixed magnetization. Once the magnetization is fixed, we can show the convergence of the enriched free energy to the solution of a Hamilton-Jacobi equation. The magnetization constraint is also used to show the convexity of the initial condition in this equation, and this yields a variational representation of the solution, as a Hopf formula. Convex duality then turns this formula into an optimization over martingales whose initial values are the prescribed magnetizations.

entries.title: Large deviations, gradient flows and fluctuating hydrodynamics for fractional diffusion
entries.abstract: This work is a step towards a general understanding of fluctuations for systems of particles described at large scale by fractional diffusion. First, we derive formally a Large Deviation Principle for the empirical measure of mean-field interacting particles with a L{é}vy-type noise. In the case of independent particles, this unveils a generalized gradient flow structure at large scales. Second, we derive and solve numerically a stochastic Partial Differential Equation describing the fluctuating hydrodynamics of this system. The results compare well with direct numerical integration of the particles' dynamics.

entries.title: Backward and reflected backward stochastic differential equations under initial enlargement of Brownian filtrations
entries.abstract: We investigate the effect of initially enlarging a Brownian filtration by its terminal value on backward stochastic differential equations (BSDEs) and reflected BSDEs (RBSDEs). We establish the Brownian innovation representation and the predictable representation property in the enlarged filtration, highlighting the singular information drift arising from the semimartingale decomposition of the original Brownian motion. We derive transfer identities under suitable integrability conditions and provide explicit counterexamples showing that the resulting singular equations may fail to admit unique square-integrable solutions, including in the reflected case. We further develop a conditional parametrization of regular BSDEs and establish a conditional comparison principle for Snell envelopes, illustrating both the strict value of additional information and the failure of general pathwise domination. An exact projection identity is also obtained for zero-driver terminal payoffs. Finally, we discuss possible extensions to irregular obstacles and more general information structures.

entries.title: Packing intermediate dimensions of measures and applications
entries.abstract: We introduce a spectrum of dimensions of measures, the \emph{packing intermediate dimensions} $\dim_{P,θ}μ$, $θ\in(0,1]$, of a Borel probability measure $μ$ on $\mathbb{R}^n$ and the \emph{quasi-Hausdorff dimension} $\dim_{qH}μ$. We show that this spectrum encodes the information on $μ$ that governs the packing dimension of its projections and Hölder images. First, $\dim_{qH}μ$ is the exact threshold for the packing dimension profiles of Falconer and Howroyd: for every real $0<s\leq n$, $\dim_P^sμ=s$ if and only if $s\leq\dim_{qH}μ$. Second, we prove a lower bound for the profiles in terms of $\dim_Hμ$, $\dim_{P,θ}μ$ and the Assouad dimension of $\operatorname{supp}μ$, which improves the bound of Falconer and Mattila, the best previously known general lower bound for the packing dimension of projected measures. The improvement is strict whenever $\dim_Hμ<\dim_Pμ$ and $\dim_A(\operatorname{supp}μ)<n$, and when $\dim_A(\operatorname{supp}μ)=n$ it occurs exactly when $\dim_{P,θ}μ$ exceeds an explicit universal lower bound for some $θ$ in an explicit range. We present examples of measures with $\dim_Hμ<\dim_Pμ<\dim_A(\operatorname{supp}μ)=n$ for which our bound gives the exact value $\dim_Pμ_V=\min\{\dim_Pμ,m\}$ for almost every $m$-dimensional subspace $V$, whereas the bound of Falconer and Mattila is strictly smaller. As applications, for a large family of random $α$-Hölder maps $f_ω:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^m$, we prove that, for compactly supported $μ$, $\dim_Pμ_{f_ω}=m$ almost surely if and only if $αm\leq\dim_{qH}μ$, and that the packing analogue of Kahane's formula holds for fractional Brownian motions if and only if $\dim_{qH}μ=\dim_Pμ$. Analogous results are obtained for analytic sets.

entries.title: Optimal Control of Mean-field FBSDEs and Classical Solutions of the Related Generalized HJB Equations
entries.abstract: In this article, we study optimal control problems driven by mean-field forward-backward stochastic differential equations (FBSDEs). The aim is two-fold: (i) to provide the unique optimal control; (ii) to establish classical solutions of the associated generalized Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman (HJB) equations on the space of probability measures. For (i), we study the coupled system arising from the maximum principle, which involves both the state FBSDEs and the adjoint FBSDEs. This system is non-standard and more complicated than that in standard mean-field type control (MFTC) problems. By extending the method of continuation in the coefficients to our framework, we establish the well-posedness result, and subsequently obtain the differentiability of the value functional with respect to the distribution argument --- thereby extending existing results for MFTC problems. For (ii), since the flow property does not generally hold for control problems of FBSDEs, standard dynamic-programming arguments cannot be applied directly. We therefore develop probabilistic approaches to the classical solvability of generalized HJB equations under three distinct sets of conditions. The auxiliary processes arising in these arguments differ significantly from those in standard MFTC problems. We establish new connections between the value function and the adjoint processes, derive equations for the relevant decoupling field, and obtain first- and second-order generalized HJB equations, including a coupled system on the space of probability measures. The standard HJB equations for MFTC problems are recovered as special cases. Our approach yields classical solutions without requiring non-degeneracy of the diffusion.

entries.title: Eigenvalue fluctuations for the crushed ice problem
entries.abstract: We study the eigenvalues of the negative Dirichlet Laplacian $-Δ$ in domain $D_{ε,N}$ obtained by removing $N$ Euclidean balls of radius $ε$ from a bounded open set $D\subseteq\mathbb R^d$ ($d\ge2$). It is known that, for the balls centered at points drawn independently from a distribution with probability density $ρ$ and for $N\to\infty$ and $ε\downarrow0$ so that the aggregate Newtonian capacity of the removed balls tends to some $κ>0$, the eigenvalues of $-Δ$ in $D_{ε,N}$ homogenize to those of the Schrödinger operator $-Δ+κρ$ in $D$. Here we prove that, for the eigenvalues that are simple in the limit, a multivariate Central Limit Theorem holds in all $d\ge2$ under centering by expected values. Unlike earlier work in $d=3$ by Figari, Orlandi and Teta and, independently, Ozawa from 1980s that was based on resolvent expansions, we rely on martingale representations and one-ball perturbation asymptotic controlled by methods of harmonic analysis.

entries.title: Optimal scaling and curvature correction for constrained MCMC on spheres
entries.abstract: Sampling Gaussian measures restricted to nonlinear manifolds in high dimensions requires a proposal kernel that respects both geometric constraints and dimensional scaling requirements. We introduce tangent preconditioned Crank-Nicolson (pCN), which combines a manifold projection with a cancellation of the ambient Gaussian contribution, leaving only a geometric residual. Considering a shifted sphere with $\sqrt d$ scaling of radius and centre as a tractable benchmark embedded manifold, we prove that uncorrected tangent pCN results in a proposal noise scale of order $d^{-1/6}$ (compared to $d^{-1/2}$ for a tangent random-walk). We establish asymptotic optimal tuning for the geodesic expected squared jump distance which is maximised at an acceptance probability of 0.574 for the family of drift-corrected tangent proposals containing tangent pCN and tangent MALA. We also prove a joint diffusion limit for the parallel and orthogonal coordinates to the sphere's centre vector of tangent pCN. The orthogonal diffusion speed matches the limiting geodesic expected squared jump distance and is maximised at acceptance probability 0.574, whereas the parallel speed is maximised at 0.712, demonstrating that optimal tuning depends on the observable. We then identify an intrinsic precision correction characterised by potential Hessian and Ricci curvature that yields a proposal kernel with dimension-independent fixed step size limit. We discuss a generalisation to arbitrary hypersurfaces and present nondegenerate scaling of tangent pCN applied to conditioned diffusions under resolution refinement.

entries.title: $L^2$ convergence rates for singular stochastic wave dynamics
entries.abstract: We establish quantitative hypocoercivity for singular stochastic damped wave equations arising in stochastic quantization. Building on the finite-dimensional argument of Cao, Lu, and Wang [Arch. Rat. Mech. Anal. 2023], we derive a dimension-free criterion that replaces uniform semiconvexity by a log-Sobolev inequality together with exponential lower-tail bounds for the bottom of the Hessian spectrum. We verify this criterion for the two-dimensional $Φ^4_2$ and sine-Gordon models and for the three-dimensional $Φ^4_3$ model, through estimates on the lowest eigenvalue of associated singular random Schrödinger operators. Combined with the continuum limit established in a companion paper, this yields exponential $L^2$ convergence to equilibrium for the $Φ^4_2$ dynamics and for sine-Gordon with $β^2<2π$. For $Φ^4_2$, we verify that in a weak-coupling, small-mass regime, optimizing the damping yields a kinetic relaxation rate of at least order $m$. This yields a genuine acceleration over the order-$m^2$ relaxation rate of the overdamped dynamics. The lattice estimates are uniform in the discretization for sine-Gordon throughout $β^2<4π$, and for $Φ^4_3$ at fixed volume, including regimes beyond those for which the continuum dynamics is vpresently constructed.

entries.title: Cutoff profiles and boundary effects in the Togashi-Kaneko model of autocatalytic reactions with weak mutations
entries.abstract: We determine explicit bulk and worst-case total variation cutoff profiles for the configuration law of a two-species Togashi--Kaneko model with a fixed population of $n$ particles and weak mutations. Boundary initial conditions introduce an additional logarithmic growth phase and change both the leading mixing-time coefficient and the limiting cutoff profile. Let $κ_1,κ_2>0$ be the autocatalytic rate constants and put $λ_*=κ_1κ_2/(κ_1+κ_2)$. For deterministic initial configurations whose density converges to $m\in(0,1)$, the total variation distance to equilibrium at time $t_n(s)=\frac{\log n}{2λ_*}+\frac{s}{λ_*}$ converges to $\mathcal G(r(m)e^{-s})$ for every fixed $s\in\mathbb R$, where $\mathcal G(r)=d_{\mathrm{TV}}(\mathcal N(r,1),\mathcal N(0,1))$, $r(m)>0$ is explicit, and $\mathcal N(a,b^2)$ denotes the Gaussian distribution with mean $a$ and variance $b^2$. For the worst-case distance $\mathscr D_n(t)$ over all initial configurations, we prove $\mathscr D_n(T_n+s/λ_*)\to\mathcal P(s)$, where $T_n=\left(\frac{1}{\min\{κ_1,κ_2\}}+\frac{1}{2λ_*}\right)\log n$.The profile $\mathcal P$ is the total variation distance between the equilibrium Gaussian and a Gaussian mixture whose random displacement is determined by a gamma-distributed amplitude arising from early growth at the boundary. Unlike the bulk profile, $\mathcal P$ depends on the mutation parameters. Both cutoffs have windows of constant order, and we identify the asymptotically worst boundary configurations.

entries.title: Sampling from the Sherrington-Kirkpatrick Model up to Criticality
entries.abstract: We prove that the simulated annealing algorithm efficiently samples from the Sherrington-Kirkpatrick model at inverse temperature $β< 1$ to an arbitrary inverse polynomial accuracy in total variation.

entries.title: Large deviation principle for determinantal point processes on Stein manifolds
entries.abstract: In this paper, we study natural determinantal point processes on Stein manifolds defined by canonical sections and plurisubharmonic weight functions. We present a natural condition on the weights under which these processes satisfy a large deviation principle with a good rate function given by the Fenchel--Legendre transform of the pluripotential equilibrium energy. Along the way, we prove some pluripotential theoretic results on Stein manifolds, such as the $C^{1,1}$ regularity of appropriate envelopes. These results are noncompact analogues of results of Berman and Berman--Boucksom on compact Kähler manifolds.

entries.title: Optimal transportation under McKean-Vlasov dynamics
entries.abstract: We study a broad class of stochastic transport problems under controlled McKean-Vlasov dynamics, allowing control of both drift and volatility, with weak terminal constraints. In contrast to the classical Schrödinger problem, the reference dynamics depend on the evolving law of the process, leading to nonlinear optimization problems on path space, while the terminal constraint is formulated through weak optimal transport, permitting a flexible treatment of distributional targets. This framework encompasses several problems of current interest, including the mean field Schrödinger problem, martingale optimal transport, and Schrödinger-Bass bridges. We establish three main results. First, we prove the existence of optimal controls under general coercivity, continuity, and convexity assumptions. Second, we derive a convex dual representation that extends weak Kantorovich duality and stochastic optimal transport duality to controlled McKean-Vlasov dynamics. Finally, for the mean field Schrödinger problem, we prove convergence, at the level of value functions, of the associated finite-particle Schrödinger bridge problems to the mean field limit, thereby identifying the nonlinear problem as the exact infinite-particle limit of finite-particle Schrödinger bridges. As a byproduct, we establish the existence of an optimal mean field Schrödinger potential, providing a variational foundation for duality in nonlinear stochastic transport.

entries.title: Alpern Lemma Independent of a Partition for Aperiodic Systems
entries.abstract: We prove that for every $(X,\mathcal{B},μ,T)$, an aperiodic, probability preserving system and $\mathcal{P}$ a finite measurable partition of $X$, there exists an Alpern Multitower whose base is independent of $\mathcal{P}$. This removes the ergodicity assumption in the original proof of the independent Alpern Lemma of \cite{MR3373823}. As a consequence, we remove ergodicity assumption from recent results on limit theorems in deterministic systems \cite{Kosloff_Volny_2022,kosloffVolnyStableCLT,MR4955410}.

entries.title: Large Deviations of Invariant Measures of Fractional Reaction-Diffusion Equations Driven by Multiplicative Noise on R^n
entries.abstract: In this paper, we establish large deviations of invariant measures for fractional stochastic reaction-diffusion equations with polynomial reaction term driven by unbounded multiplicative noise on R^n. Under a dissipativity condition, we first prove the Freidlin-Wentzell large deviation principle of solution trajectories uniformly over all initial data in L^2(R^n). The key ingredient is a positive-time L^\infty-estimate for differences of controlled solutions which is independent of all initial data and hence yields uniform convergence of controlled stochastic solutions over the entire tphase space. Then using the uniform trajectory estimates, contraction and a second-moment estimate, we further prove the large deviations of invariant measures of the equation with a good quasipotential without introducing weighted spaces or establishing exponential tightness. The non-compactness of Sobolev embeddings in R^n is circumvented by uniform spatial tail-ends estimates. This is the first result on large deviations of invariant measures of the equation with multiplicative noise on unbounded domains.

entries.title: Limit Theorems for the Complete Feedback Card Guessing Game
entries.abstract: We study the optimal score $T_{n,m}$ in a complete feedback card guessing game. The deck has $n$ types and $m$ cards of each type. Its predictable compensator $S_{n,m}$ is the sum of the conditional success probabilities. We prove that Var$(S_{n,m})\leq C((\log\log n)^2+m/\log n)$, uniformly in $m$ for large $n$. This bound yields a central limit theorem for every sequence $m=m_n\geq1$ as $n\to\infty$. The score variance is asymptotic to its mean. We also give uniform Kolmogorov bounds using the conditional Bernoulli moments. For $m,n\to\infty$, the excess mean is asymptotic to $(\log n)\log\min\{m,\log n\}+(π/\sqrt2)\sqrt{m\log n}$. The two contributions balance at $m\asymp(\log n)(\log\log n)^2$. The variance proof uses reversed occupancy hitting times. Discrete hypergeometric tail estimates control their fluctuations in the large-deviation, Gaussian, and saturation regimes. For fixed $n$, we also show that the compensator has a Brownian-bridge functional limit as $m\to\infty$.

entries.title: Optimal Feature-Based Newsvendor Policies under Censored Demand
entries.abstract: We investigate a newsvendor problem where a decision-maker observes a $z$-dimensional vector of covariates, and wants to learn how much stock to order given a sample of size $n$ of censored demand data to minimize costs. Demand is censored when insufficient stock is available to meet it, and past stocking quantities are known. We propose a new model-agnostic loss function approach to estimate optimal order quantities using observational data, and characterize the optimal newsvendor policy as the policy that minimizes our proposed loss function. Our method requires only a single estimation step, can be scaled to datasets with hundreds of thousands of data points, and does not suffer from the same instabilities as inverse censoring probability weighting methods. We describe how this loss function can be implemented in linear empirical risk minimization, kernel weights optimization and deep neural network algorithms, and provide excess risk generalization bounds for their out-of-sample performance. Moreover, we show through numerical experiments that our method quickly converges to the optimal policy on synthetic data, and leads to improved performance on real world retail data.

entries.title: Delta functions, a local coarea formula and marginal distributions
entries.abstract: We define multidimensional delta functions as generalized functions by pulling back the Dirac delta function, as well as products of such. We prove various formulas including a local version of the coarea formula and we use delta functions to compute marginal probability distributions on spheres.

entries.title: Large Network limit for Latent Variable Process Models with Endogeneously Evolving Interactions among Multiple Types
entries.abstract: Motivated by the opinion and social dynamics literature, we rigorously study dynamically co-evolving latent space network models, where agent opinions evolve based on a latent state space model influenced by and influencing an underlying dynamically evolving graph determining their interactions. In contrast to earlier work, see [18], agents are allowed to be heterogeneous, i.e., of different types, and their dynamic evolution can capture behaviors like attraction and repulsion between and within groups. In addition, the model encodes bidirectional feedback between the latent process and the underlying interaction network, persistence effects are included, and the interactions are localized, i.e., individual agents do not have global information. We produce weak and empirical limit theorems that encode the asymptotic joint distribution of agent opinion trajectories and their interaction network. In doing so, we describe and exploit the complex dependence structure of the model.

entries.title: DynaSPLIT: Strong tail-optimal scheduling for the M/G/n with heavy-tailed job sizes
entries.abstract: We study the asymptotic response time tail in the M/G/n queue with heavy-tailed (regularly varying) job sizes. For this setting, strongly tail optimal policies are known only at lower load, where n-1 servers suffice for stability. At higher load, the tail optimal scheduling has been open. This paper presents DynaSPLIT, the first strongly tail optimal policy at high load. Together with prior work, this result shows that strong tail optimality is achievable across the entire stability region of the M/G/n with heavy-tailed job sizes.

entries.title: Kinetic SDEs and kinetic Fokker-Planck equations with critical Morrey-type drifts, and local blow-ups
entries.abstract: We develop a Sobolev theory for the kinetic Fokker-Planck equation subject to a singular Morrey-form $L^\infty+M^q_K$ force field which can produce local blow-ups due to strong attraction to a submanifold. Our approach is based on the fractional representation for the Duhamel series of the equation and on establishing kinetic Adams-type estimates. Accordingly, we construct weak solutions of Brownian-driven kinetic SDEs in a critical Morrey set-up, obtain kinetic Krylov-type estimates and a strongly continuous Feller propagator, and establish uniqueness criteria for a large class of weak solutions.

entries.title: Reach-Avoid Certificates for Contact-based Stochastic Hybrid Systems
entries.abstract: This work studies certified reach-avoid control of stochastic hybrid systems in which a stochastic differential equation governs continuous flow and a controlled stochastic kernel governs guard-triggered resets. The input appears only in the reset kernel, where it determines the post-jump distribution. Certificates for such systems have so far assumed spontaneous or controller-chosen jump times, a finite horizon, or discrete-time dynamics; we certify, over the infinite horizon, that the target is reached before the unsafe set with at least a prescribed probability. First, we introduce reach-avoid contact certificates, whose flow and jump conditions are imposed only on a sublevel corridor, and prove that any such certificate with a compatible reset policy meets the specification; a pointwise safety filter extends this guarantee from verification to control by constraining arbitrary nominal controllers. Next, we prove that executions are non-Zeno and bound the expected settling time and reset count. We frame certificate search as a linear program over any twice-differentiable dictionary followed by independent verification. We illustrate our approach via comparisons where the certified region is a subset covering 93.6\% of the ground truth and where our certificate-based safety filter reaches the goal while reducing collisions from 68 to zero across 200 episodes of a dribbling ball problem.

entries.title: Higher-Order Paracontrolled Calculus for Geometric Rough Paths
entries.abstract: We study the rough differential equation $$ \frac{du_t}{dt}= F(u_t) ζ_t, \ \ u(0) = u_0 \in \mathbb{R}^d, $$ where $F : \mathbb{R}^d \to L(\mathbb{R}^d, \mathbb{R}^d)$ is a sufficiently regular vector field, and the noise $ζ$ is a distribution in $\mathscr{C}^{α-1}(\mathbb{R})$ for $α\in (\frac{1}{4}, \frac{1}{3})$. We construct solutions to this equation at lower regularity than previous work of Gubinelli-Imkeller-Perkowski and Prömel-Trabs using ideas from the high-order paracontrolled viewpoint of Bailleul-Bernicot. The key tool in our work is the development of a harmonic-analytic framework for proving a set of iterated commutator estimates which are necessary for the solution theory. We also show the procedure of enhancement when the noise $ζ= dZ$, where $Z$ is a realization of fractional Brownian motion with Hurst parameter $H \in (\frac{1}{4}, \frac{1}{3})$.

entries.title: Ideal Poisson--Voronoi tessellations for Finsler metrics on symmetric spaces
entries.abstract: Ideal Poisson--Voronoi tessellations are random tessellations that arise as limits of Voronoi diagrams for Poisson point processes as their intensity tends to zero. For the Riemannian metric on a symmetric space of higher rank, Frączyk, Mellick, and Wilkens (arXiv:2307.01194) proved that the corresponding ideal Poisson--Voronoi tessellation is almost surely completely connected, with an unbounded side between any two cells. This contrasts sharply with the geometry of ideal Poisson--Voronoi tessellations in hyperbolic spaces studied by D'Achille, Curien, Enriquez, Lyons, and Ünel (arXiv:2303.16831). In this paper we introduce and study ideal Poisson--Voronoi tessellations for Finsler metrics on higher rank symmetric spaces. We show that ideal Poisson--Voronoi tessellations with respect to polyhedral Finsler metrics can exhibit either behavior seen in these previous works: generically they resemble the hyperbolic case, where almost surely all cells have bounded sides. We further introduce the ideal Selberg--Poisson--Voronoi tessellation of the space of positive definite symmetric matrices, which has particularly nice properties.

entries.title: On the Stability of the Independence Number of the Distance Graph G(n,r,<s) for Growing r and s
entries.abstract: We consider a random subgraph G_p(n,r,<s) of the complete distance graph G(n,r,<s) whose vertices are the r-element subsets of the set {1,...,n} and whose edges join pairs of subsets that intersect in fewer than s elements; each edge survives independently of the others with probability p. The stability of the Erdos-Ko-Rado theorem is the event that the independence number of the random subgraph equals that of the original graph, N = C_{n-s}^{r-s}. For fixed r and s, two-sided bounds for the critical probability, whose ratio depends on r and s, were obtained by P. A. Ogarok and A. M. Raigorodskii. In this paper we establish the order of the critical probability for growing r=r(n) and s=s(n): if min{C_r^s r^2, s r^3} = o(n), then the upper and lower bounds differ only by an absolute constant factor. The proof is elementary; only one of the two branches of the growth condition uses the complete nontrivial-intersection theorem of Ahlswede-Khachatrian.

entries.title: Entropy, isoperimetry and the total variation profile of random walks
entries.abstract: The total variation profile $\mathrm{TV}_n$ of a random walk measures how far its distribution at time $n$ is from being invariant under the generators. Three lower bounds are given: an elementary bound $\mathrm{TV}_n \geq 1/\big(44\,L(n)\big)$ in terms of the speed $L(n)$; a bound by the entropy increment $H(P^{n+1}) - H(P^n)$, which is a reverse Pinsker inequality; and a bound in terms of the entropy and the isoperimetric profile. Deciding whether the entropy-increment bound always improves on the isoperimetric one is related to conjectures on the growth of the entropy and of groups. The motivation comes from the question of whether the distributions of a random walk can be transported back onto their translates at bounded cost.

entries.title: Very high genus double Hurwitz numbers via mixing times
entries.abstract: We obtain very high genus asymptotics for double Hurwitz numbers when both the size $n$ and the genus $g$ go to infinity, under the constraint that $g$ grows much faster than $n$, more precisely that $\frac{2g}{n}-\ln n\to\infty$. Our proof relies on adapting arguments about the mixing time of the transposition random walk introduced by Diaconis and Shahshahani.

entries.title: Classical and Quantum Information Measures Characterizing Convertibility: An Axiomatic Approach
entries.abstract: In this PhD thesis, we take an axiomatic approach to studying multivariate divergences, which are measures of the information content of a tuple of classical or quantum states. These divergences are studied in the context of large-sample and catalytic convertibility of tuples of states. This type of convertibility is characterized by the ordering of an axiomatically defined family of divergences. In this thesis, we identify this family of divergences explicitly for two scenarios, one classical and one quantum. In the classical setting, we show that the relevant divergences are certain generalizations of the bivariate Rényi divergences. Unlike previous studies, we do not require the distributions to have the same support, yielding interesting new divergences. In the quantum setting, we consider pairs of classical-quantum states with pure component states, and find that majorization is characterized by all $α$-$z$ relative entropies for $α<1$. This demonstrates the first operational interpretation of these relative entropies.

entries.title: A Generalized Elephant Random Walk with Time-Dependent Memory
entries.abstract: The elephant random walk (ERW) is a discrete-time random walk with complete memory. At every step the walker chooses one of the previous increments at random and then either repeats with a constant probability $p\in [0,1]$ or reverses it. Since its introduction by Schütz and Trimper, the model has become a useful probabilistic framework for studying long-range dependence, anomalous diffusion, reinforcement, and phase transitions. This paper proposes a generalized ERW model with time-dependent memory. In this generalized model, the usual constant memory parameter $p$ in the standard ERW is allowed to change with time. The cental limit theorems, and the law of the iterated logarithm and some other strong laws are obtained.

entries.title: Sharp Rogers--Shephard Inequalities for Rényi Entropy
entries.abstract: We establish sharp weighted Rogers--Shephard inequalities for Rényi differential entropy. For independent copies $X,X'$ of a log-concave random vector in $\R^n$, we prove $h_p(aX-bX')\le h_p(X)+n\log(a+b)$ for all $a,b>0$ and $1\le p\le\infty$, where orders $1$ and $\infty$ correspond to Shannon entropy and min-entropy, respectively. The Shannon case settles the entropic Rogers--Shephard conjecture of Madiman and Kontoyiannis and its higher-dimensional formulation. For $1\le p<\infty$, equality holds precisely for invertible affine images of random vectors with independent exponential coordinates. At $p=\infty$, the larger equality class is characterized by possibly extended-valued convex potentials that are positively homogeneous of degree one. For every $0<p<1$, uniform laws on sufficiently high-dimensional simplices violate the unweighted bound. Thus $p=1$ is the critical order for this bound to hold in every dimension. The proof combines weighted convex intersections with an exponential lift to a log-affine probability density. At the Shannon endpoint, this lift yields an exact deficit decomposition with a conditional mutual information term for an additive channel with asymmetric Laplace noise.

entries.title: Upper tail large deviation for the first passage time in the frog model on $Z^d$ with $d\geq 2$
entries.abstract: We study upper tail large deviations for the first passage time in the frog model on $\mathbb Z^d$, $d\ge 2$. Let $\mathrm{T}(0,x)$ denote the first time at which the infection, started from the origin, reaches $x$, and let $μ$ be the associated time constant. We prove that, for any Euclidean unit vector $v\in\mathbb R^d$ and $ξ>0$, \[ \lim_{n\to\infty} -\frac{1}{\mathfrak{s}_d(n)} \log \mathbb{P}\bigl(\mathrm{T}(0,\lfloor nv\rfloor) \ge (μ(v)+ξ)n\bigr) =\mathfrak{r}_dξ, \] where $\mathfrak s_2(n)=n/\log n$ and $\mathfrak r_2=π$ for $d=2$; $\mathfrak s_d(n)=n$ and $\mathfrak r_d$ is the escape probability of simple random walk for $d\ge3$. Moreover, on the upper tail large deviation event, we show that a certain slowdown mechanism occurs near the endpoint. To rule out other mechanisms, we analyze the growth of the infection near the starting point using a modified exploration process, and investigate its propagation through the intermediate region using the renormalization and covering arguments.

entries.title: Variance Bounds for Minimum Perfect Matching Problem by Random Walk on Multinomial Distribution
entries.abstract: We establish variance upper bounds for the minimum perfect matching problem in general metric spaces under a geometric partition condition. As a principal application, let $H_n$ be the minimum perfect matching cost of $n$ independent uniform points in $[0,1]^d$, where $n$ is even and $d\ge2$. We prove $$\operatorname{Var}(H_n)\le C d n^{1-2/d},$$ where $C$ is independent of $n$ and $d$. This removes the logarithmic losses in earlier upper bounds in every dimension (Talagrand, 1995); in particular, the variance remains bounded in dimension two, answering an open question (Rhee, 1994). The proof relies on constructing a rapidly mixing Markov process with a multinomial stationary distribution.

entries.title: Fluctuations of the quadratic matching cost on the flat torus: dimensions five and higher
entries.abstract: We prove a central limit theorem for the quadratic matching cost between the uniform measure and its empirical counterpart on the flat torus in dimensions $d\ge5$. Let $μ$ be Haar probability measure on $\mathbb{T}^d$ and let $μ_n$ be the empirical measure of $n$ independent samples from $μ$. Then $$ \begin{aligned} \frac{W_2^2(μ_n,μ)-\mathbb{E}W_2^2(μ_n,μ)} {\sqrt{\operatorname{Var}(W_2^2(μ_n,μ))}} &\Longrightarrow N(0,1),\\ c_dn^{-1-4/d} \le \operatorname{Var}(W_2^2(μ_n,μ)) &\le C_dn^{-1-4/d}, \end{aligned} $$ for positive constants $c_d,C_d$ depending only on $d$ and all sufficiently large $n$. The proof introduces a random-walk approach to matching fluctuations. We construct a random walk that jumps between neighboring cells of the optimal partition and use it to describe how the matching cost responds to changes in the sample. Estimates for this walk control the effect of replacing one sample point and the interaction between two replacements. These bounds yield the variance estimates and allow us to apply a martingale central limit theorem.

entries.title: Finite-order exponential mixing does not imply the central limit theorem
entries.abstract: We show that finite-order exponential mixing does not imply the central limit theorem for smooth diffeomorphisms. For every integer $R\geq2$, we construct a $\mathcal{C}^{\infty}$ diffeomorphism $T:M\to M$ of a compact smooth manifold $M$ and a $T$-invariant probability measure $μ$ such that $(T,μ)$ is exponentially mixing of order $R$ for $\mathcal{C}^1(M)$ observables, but not of order $2R+2$. For some centred observable $f_0\in\mathcal{C}^{\infty}(M)$, no subsequence of the normalised sums $\frac{1}{\sqrt n}\sum_{i=0}^{n-1}f_0\circ T^i$ converges in distribution to a Gaussian law. In particular, exponential decay of two-point correlations implies neither exponential mixing of all orders nor the central limit theorem. We realise $(T,μ)$ in two ways. In the first, $T$ is a fixed linear Anosov diffeomorphism of $\mathbb T^2$ and $μ$ is singular with respect to Lebesgue measure. In the second, $M$ can be any compact smooth surface without boundary and $μ$ is a physical measure whose statistical basin contains a nonempty open set. The main theorems have been formalised in Lean 4.

entries.title: Hölder regularity of the top Lyapunov exponent for random matrix products with low-dimensional equator
entries.abstract: We investigate the regularity of Lyapunov exponents for products of random invertible matrices of arbitrary dimension $d\ge 2$. We prove that the top Lyapunov exponent is pointwise Hölder continuous with respect to the Wasserstein-Hausdorff distance in the space of probability measures with compact support, in the case where this exponent is simple and the equator has dimension equal to or less than one.

entries.title: On the foundations of logic and probability, II. Modal probability spaces
entries.abstract: A class of models which brings to the fore the inner logic of the calculus of probability instead of assigning probabilities to sentences is introduced and investigated.

entries.title: Discrete total variation under the multinomial, Part 2: variance under the uniform null
entries.abstract: For the counts $(X_1,\dots,X_n)\sim\mathrm{Mult}(N;1/n,\dots,1/n)$ of $N$ observations in $n$ ordered bins we study the variance of the discrete total variation $d=\sum_{i=1}^{n-1}|X_{i+1}-X_i|$. An exact decomposition splits $\mathrm{Var}(d)$ into per-edge, adjacent-pair and disjoint-pair terms and yields, for fixed $n$ as $N\to\infty$, $\mathrm{Var}(d)/N=α(n)-β(n)/N+γ(n)/N^2+o(N^{-2})$. For every $n\ge 2$, $Nα(n)$ is the classical normal-theory variance (Hoel, Kamat) of the sum of absolute successive differences of $n$ independent $N(0,N/n)$ variables; the correction $β(n)$ is obtained in closed form for $n\ge 3$ (the case $n=2$ is treated separately). Two disjoint edge differences $D_1=X_2-X_1$ and $D_3=X_4-X_3$ are exactly uncorrelated and asymptotically independent, yet $\mathrm{Cov}(|D_1|,|D_3|)=-1/(πn)+O(1/N)$: a correlation of relative order $1/N$, invisible in the Gaussian limit and absent under Poissonized sampling, whose constant is proportional to the exact joint fourth cumulant $κ_{2,2}(D_1,D_3)=-4N/n^2$ and is proved here on the lattice. The adjacent pair contributes the lattice-Edgeworth constant $a_*=-2\sqrt{3}/(9π)$, of which one quarter is a smooth Edgeworth term and three quarters a lattice-corner term; the disjoint skeleton $h(m)$ is closed through a Bessel generating function; and $γ(n)$ ($n\ge 5$) is expressed through a single triangular-lattice constant whose closed form we conjecture. Together with the mean of Part 1, the variance supplies the two moments used by moment-matched approximations to the null law of $d$. This is Part 2 of a series; the cyclic statistic $d^{c}$ will be treated in Part 5.

entries.title: Half-space polynuclear growth: a multipoint Fredholm--Pfaffian formula
entries.abstract: We derive a Fredholm-Pfaffian formula for the one-time multi-point transition probabilities of half-space polynuclear growth with any nonnegative boundary nucleation rate and general deterministic upper semi-continuous initial profiles. We prove the formula by showing that it satisfies an integral Kolmogorov equation with a unique bounded solution. We also discuss the formal 1:2:3 scaling limit of the kernel and its relation to the half-space KPZ fixed point.

entries.title: A quantitative CLT for the zeros of random trigonometric polynomials
entries.abstract: Let $X_N(t)$, $t\in[0,π]$, be a stationary Gaussian trigonometric polynomial, and let $\mathcal Z_N$ denote the number of zeros of the rescaled process $X_N(t/N)$ on $[0,Nπ]$. We establish the quantitative central limit theorem \[ d_{\mathrm W}\left( \frac{\mathcal Z_N-\mathbb E[\mathcal Z_N]} {\sqrt{\operatorname{Var}(\mathcal Z_N)}},Z\right) \le C\frac{(\log N)^2}{\sqrt N}, \] where $Z$ is standard Gaussian and $d_{\mathrm W}$ denotes the Wasserstein-1 distance. The proof combines Ornstein--Uhlenbeck regularization of the singular Kac representation with direct estimates of the covariance between the Malliavin--Stein factor and Stein test functions. A lattice lower bound of order $N^{-1/2}$ shows that the convergence rate is optimal up to logarithmic factors.

entries.title: Determinantal linear spanning forests
entries.abstract: We introduce a determinantal linear process on the space of $1$-forms over a weighted graph endowed with a unitary local system, which we call the determinantal linear spanning forest (DLSF). This process is the analog of the uniform spanning tree in the presence of an arbitrary rank $n$ quenched gauge field in ${\rm U}(n)$ (or ${\rm O}(n)$, ${\rm SO}(n)$, ${\rm SU}(n)$, ${\rm Sp}(n)$), and generalizes the determinantal random cycle-rooted spanning forest which corresponds to the case of ${\rm U}(1)$ and ${\rm SU}(2)$. We describe the support of this process by means of a polymatroid which is described in terms of the circular and bicircular matroids. We also explain how the DLSF relates to the computation of currents in an electrical network in the presence of a gauge field. The partition function of the DLSF is shown to be the determinant of the twisted Laplacian, for which we also give a matrix-tree type theorem that computes its characteristic polynomial. We initiate the study of the twisted Laplacian determinant as a functional on the space of connections, and give a first order expansion of it in a neighborhood of the trivial connection, for which we provide a probabilistic interpretation. We extend the construction to infinite graphs, exhibiting the analogs of the classical wired and free distributions on spanning forests. We give a sufficient geometric condition on the local spectral gap for the existence of a Poincaré inequality as well as the uniqueness of the infinite volume measure, and the exponential decay of correlations. We show that on any recurrent graph, the wired and free DLSF coincide. We construct examples where they do not, for example, unlike in the classical case, on $\mathbb Z^d$ for $d\geq 3$.

entries.title: Exponential profiles for the intrinsic volumes of Orlicz balls
entries.abstract: An Orlicz ball is the set of points where the sum of a fixed even convex function of the coordinates does not exceed a given radius, here proportional to the dimension. For a broad class of such functions, including non-homogeneous ones, we find the exponential rate of the intrinsic volumes whose order is proportional to the dimension and express it by a two-parameter variational formula involving only one-dimensional integrals. As a function of the order-to-dimension ratio, this rate is concave and continuous on the closed unit interval, and the convergence is uniform in the order. This proves the exponential-profile conjecture of Kabluchko, Marynych, and Prochno for these bodies and recovers their result for $\ell_p$ balls with $p>1$. The proof relies on the theory of large deviations. An exact formula for the Laplace transform of the intrinsic volumes in the radius, extending theirs for $\ell_p$ balls, plays the role of a moment generating function, and a Laplace method gives its exponential rate. An exponential change of measure, analogous to that used in Cramér's theorem, then recovers the intrinsic volumes. The key step is a lower bound on the tilted density at its mean, obtained from log-concavity rather than a law of large numbers.

entries.title: Regularity theory for lattice based harmonic maps and low temperature Gibbs measures of the spin-$O(N)$ model
entries.abstract: The purpose of this note is twofold. First, we revisit the classical regularity theory of harmonic maps in the setting of maps defined on a lattice $\mathbb{Z}^d$ instead of $\mathbb{R}^d$ or some other manifold. The target space of our harmonic maps will be spheres $\mathbb{S}^{N-1}, N\geq 2$. A harmonic map $σ: \mathbb{Z}^d \to \mathbb{S}^{N-1}$ is a map which in any finite subgraph $Λ$ minimizes the internal Dirichlet energy $\frac 1 2 \sum_{i \sim j \in Λ} \|σ_i -σ_j\|^2$ given the boundary condition $σ_{|\partial Λ}$. One key difference between our setting and the continuum is that our main Hölder regularity statement in a large domain $Λ\subset \mathbb{Z}^{d=2}$ does not require any regularity assumption on the map $σ$ restricted to the boundary of the domain. For example, when $d=2$ and $N=3$, the Hölder regularity induced in the bulk of the domain holds uniformly in all boundary configurations $σ\in (\mathbb{S}^{2})^{\partial Λ}$ (this is in contrast with the continuum which requires extensions in suitable Sobolev spaces). The fact we obtain results uniformly in the boundary conditions allows us to extend our results for positive temperatures. Namely, as $T \searrow 0$, we obtain a local regularity theory for all infinite volume Spin $O(N)$ Gibbs measures, at least when $d=2$ and $N\geq 3$. We also discuss implications of our analysis in dimensions $d\geq 3$.

entries.title: Revisiting the Bobkov-Chistyakov-Götze theorem on approximately Gaussian marginals
entries.abstract: We study one-dimensional marginals of an isotropic, log-concave probability measure in $\mathbb{R}^n$. We show that the Kolmogorov distance between a typical marginal and the standard Gaussian distribution is at most $C/n$, for a universal constant $C > 0$. This bound is optimal in general, up to the value of the universal constant. It improves the Gaussian approximation bound of Bobkov, Chistyakov and Götze by a logarithmic factor in the log-concave setting.

entries.title: GROMM: Generative Risk-neutral Option Market Models
entries.abstract: We present a statically and dynamically arbitrage-free European option market model with smooth interpolation between option prices, based on the SANOS framework, and prove that its dynamics admit a unique strong solution. In spirit, it is a stochastic model for local volatility when the latter is used as a representation of a European option price surface, not as a pricing model. We illustrate the strength of our approach on S&P Index Option data from January 2022 to August 2025. We show that the model's initial state fits within bid/ask for more than 95% of relevant market option prices. We then train the model dynamics under $\mathbb{P}$ and $\mathbb{Q}$ and show that the model is indeed free of arbitrage while fitting the dynamics of the market well. We also propose a range of BHW-tests to test for absence of arbitrage.

entries.title: Averaged Annealed Markov Chains Achieve the Algorithmic Threshold for Tensor PCA, Part I: Glauber Dynamics
entries.abstract: In the tensor principal components analysis (tensor PCA) problem, we are asked to recover an unknown vector in $\{\pm1\}^N$ from a noisy observation of its $k$-th tensor power, for a fixed $k\ge3$. Tensor PCA exhibits a well-studied information-computation gap: global algorithms such as spectral methods and sum-of-squares work above an algorithmic threshold, below which we know matching lower bounds (against these and some other restricted models of computation). In contrast, local algorithms such as Markov chains were only known to succeed from a random initialization at a polynomially larger signal-to-noise ratio, and were believed to be inferior to global algorithms for tensor PCA. We show that Glauber dynamics, when supplemented with annealing and ergodic averaging, achieves polynomial-time strong recovery above the algorithmic threshold from a uniformly random initialization, demonstrating that local Markov chains can succeed all the way down to the algorithmic threshold from an uninformative cold start.

entries.title: The relation between non-exchangeability and radial asymmetry of copulas
entries.abstract: Non-exchangeability and radial asymmetry have got substantial attention in the literature, but relation between the two has not been studied yet. We propose the question: if a copula has a given degree of radial asymmetry, what is the range of possible values of the measure of non-exhangeability. We determine the set of all points whose first coordinate is the radial asymmetry of a copula and the second coordinate is its non-exchangeability. We show that this set is a non-convex hexagon.

entries.title: Closed-form evaluation of the cumulative distribution function and absolute moments of the variance-gamma distribution
entries.abstract: Closed-form formulas are derived for the cumulative distribution function and odd-order absolute moments of the variance-gamma distribution. As a special case, closed-form expressions are deduced for the cumulative distribution function and odd-order absolute central moments of the product of two correlated zero-mean normal random variables.

entries.title: Dudley-type bound for stationary Bernoulli processes
entries.abstract: This is preliminary, AI-generated note on the Dudley-type bound for stationary Bernoulli processes postulated by M. Talagrand based on the unpublished notes of the authors and the recent note \cite{invariant} which in turn is an alternative proof of the result by Hu, Wang, Wu.

entries.title: Poincaré inequalities, logarithmic growth and doubling
entries.abstract: We investigate when a Poincaré inequality forces the underlying measure to be doubling, with particular attention to the space \(X\) controlling the oscillation. We identify \(L\log L\) as the sharp threshold: under a natural local growth condition on the measure, doubling is forced precisely when \(L\log L(0,1)\not\hookrightarrow X\). We also obtain a doubling criterion under a weaker geometric assumption when the oscillation norm is sufficiently stronger than \(L\log L\). We show that this threshold is sharp in every fixed Euclidean dimension, using a dimension-free local \(L\log L\)-Poincaré inequality for log-concave measures and non-doubling Gaussian examples. We then turn to infinite-dimensional spaces, where doubling is impossible for the measures under consideration. Nevertheless, the \(L\log L\)-Poincaré inequality continues to hold, and we establish sharp characterizations for infinite product models, Gaussian measures on Hilbert spaces under power-type small-ball estimates, and Wiener measure with the uniform norm.

entries.title: Axioms and internal rigidity of spectral duality structures
entries.abstract: Spectral duality structures (SDS) explain why a distinguished family of initial distributions makes the absorption probabilities of resetting processes insensitive to the resetting mechanism. Here we study their axioms. We prove that the six defining conditions are mutually independent and determine what each one contributes. The key tool is a structure theorem valid for an arbitrary permutation and an arbitrary positive weight: every insensitive distribution is supported on a union of cycles balanced at a common level, and the level of a cycle is fixed by the geometric mean of the weight on it. From it, positivity selects the admissible root, the constant orbit product is equivalent to the existence of an insensitive distribution of full support, and the involution is equivalent to the response rank being equal to the number of free weight parameters. Without the duality relation, insensitivity of a single distribution is cheap and generically isolated; duality turns it into structural neutrality of the separatrix. The full-rank condition splits into two layers: a weaker condition is equivalent to maximal response rank, while full rank also excludes insensitivity at any other level. We then show that a single SDS is internally rigid: compatible semigroup structures force a constant weight, compatible abelian group structures obey a precise arithmetic condition, congruences form a simple lattice, and the automorphism group is computed explicitly. Finally, the axioms do not determine the orientation of the response; in the two-site case we give the exact condition under which the geometric and analytic sign criteria agree.

entries.title: $\mathcal{D}$-Pullback Measure Attractors of McKean-Vlasov Stochastic Lattice Wave Equations
entries.abstract: This paper deals with the pullback measure attractor for a non-autonomous distribution-dependent stochastic lattice wave equation with nonlinear noise on $\mathbb{Z}$. We establish well-posedness in the energy space $\ell^{2}\times\ell^{2}$ and show that the solution generates a continuous non-autonomous dynamical system on $\mathcal{P}_{4}(\ell^{2}\times\ell^{2})$, which possesses a unique pullback measure attractor $\mathcal{A}$. Furthermore, we prove the convergence of the attractor $\mathcal{A}^{\varepsilon}$ as $\varepsilon\to 0^{+}$ to the attractor of the corresponding distribution-independent limit system.

entries.title: Large deviation principles for 2D stochastic $g$-Navier--Stokes equations on unbounded channel-like domains
entries.abstract: This paper investigates the large deviation principle for 2D stochastic $g$-Navier--Stokes equations driven by multiplicative noise and defined on an unbounded channel-like domain. We first prove the existence and uniqueness of probabilistically strong solutions for the stochastic equation under small noise perturbations by means of the local monotonicity method. Subsequently, we show the well-posedness of solutions to the corresponding control equation and the convergence in distribution of the solutions for the stochastic equation as the noise intensity tends to zero. Finally, we establish the Freidlin-Wentzell type large deviation principle for the solutions of the stochastic equation by using the weak convergence method. To overcome the lack of compactness of Sobolev embedding on unbounded domains, we employ a scalar stream function together with a truncation technique to derive uniform tail estimates for the solutions of the control equation.

entries.title: Distinguishing sets and measures from their planar Brownian images
entries.abstract: Motivated by a question of Hochman, we investigate whether two deterministic time measures or time sets can be distinguished almost surely from a single planar Brownian image. Using rescaled correlation integrals, we give a criterion for mutual singularity of the laws of the image measures, even when the time measures have the same dimension. For self-similar time sets satisfying the open set condition, we also recover the natural occupation measure from the compact image. Together, these results allow us to distinguish lattice and non-lattice self-similar sets and their natural measures within this class. For a naturally parametrised family with two contractions, with fixed dimension, each parameter can be distinguished from all but finitely many others. If the dimension is sufficiently small, every distinct parameter can be distinguished.

entries.title: Optimal information loss for Liouville spectral responses
entries.abstract: We study Fisher information about the amplitude of a known smooth mean shift from the first Dirichlet eigenvalue and spatial responses of a Liouville random medium. The complete response record determines the speed measure and the Gaussian free field, whereas every finite record strictly loses information; an optimal design exists in each finite-dimensional probe space. We quantify this gap as the known Liouville parameter $γ$ tends to zero. If the probe space contains an explicit matching probe, the minimum loss equals $γ^2$ times a positive compression error for a deterministic second-chaos operator, up to $o(γ^2)$, with designs allowed to depend on $γ$. After enlarging the probe dictionary, the optimal $m$-response coefficient is asymptotic to $\|Lg\|_{L^1(D)}^2/(8m)$, where $L=-(2π)^{-1}Δ_D$ on the unit disk $D$. A quadratic correction of the readouts attains the same fixed-design loss to second order.

entries.title: Limiting distributions of the rightmost eigenvalue of the truncated circular Unitary ensemble across all truncation regimes
entries.abstract: We study the limiting distribution of the largest real part of the eigenvalues of truncated unitary matrices. Let \(U_m\) be an \(m\times m\) Haar-distributed unitary matrix, and let \(Z_1,\ldots,Z_n\) be the eigenvalues of its upper-left \(n\times n\) principal submatrix. We determine the limiting distribution of \(\max_{1\le i\le n}\Re Z_i\) under a unified normalization: the limiting law is Gumbel when $q:=m-n\to\infty$ and is of Weibull type when $q$ is fixed. The fixed-\(q\) limiting laws converge to the Gumbel law as \(q\to\infty\). We also give a unified formulation of the normalizing constants for the spectral radius that recovers the previously known limiting laws.

entries.title: Regularity lemma for Gaussian polynomials
entries.abstract: We prove a regularity lemma for polynomials with fixed degree $d$ and any number of standard Gaussian input variables. Following modern approaches to the Szemer{é}di regularity lemma, we deduce our results from a general formulation of the regularity lemma using ultraproducts. Along the way, we give a direct combinatorial proof of the celebrated ``fourth moment theorem'' of Nualart and Peccati, which characterizes the asymptotically Gaussian polynomials inside degree-$d$ Gaussian chaos as those such that $\mathbb{E} p^2 \to 1$ and $\mathbb{E} p^4 \to 3$.

entries.title: Wasserstein rates of all orders for the Sato-Tate law of Kloosterman sums
entries.abstract: Let $μ_q$ be the distribution of the normalized Kloosterman sums $\mathrm{Kl}(a;q)$, $a\in\mathbb{F}_q^\times$, and let $μ_{\mathrm{ST}}$ be the Sato--Tate law. We prove $W_s(μ_q,μ_{\mathrm{ST}})\ll q^{-1/3}$ for $1\le s\le2$, $W_s(μ_q,μ_{\mathrm{ST}})\ll q^{-1/6-1/(3s)}$ for $2\le s<\infty$, and $W_\infty(μ_q,μ_{\mathrm{ST}})\ll q^{-1/6}$, answering a question of Kowalski and Untrau. More generally, we bound $W_s(μ,μ_{\mathrm{ST}})$ for all $s$ whenever the Chebyshev moments of $μ$ satisfy bounds of Katz type. For $s=2$ the bound also follows from a smoothing inequality of Borda and Cuenin; for $s>2$ and $s=\infty$ our bounds are stronger. The proof uses the quantile coupling, which arises from Stieltjes sums over two different intervals whose cells are paired so as to balance two measures, and which is optimal for all $s$ simultaneously; an explicit $W_2$ smoothing inequality relative to $μ_{\mathrm{ST}}$; and a sharp comparison between $W_s$ and the Kolmogorov distance for laws with square-root edges. The last result shows that $q^{-1/6}$ is the best rate for $W_\infty$ obtainable from Niederreiter's discrepancy bound. Numerically, for primes $10^3<p<10^6$, all these distances appear to decay like $p^{-1/2}$.

entries.title: Fourier entropy of threshold functions and their compositions
entries.abstract: We prove the Fourier entropy--influence inequality for every linear threshold function, with a constant below $8.937$ and no restrictions on its weights or threshold. The argument applies to regular Boolean functions and gives logarithmic bounds for their Boolean combinations and for unions with bounded variable overlap. Character multiplication preserves the estimates and yields bounds by influence minus variance. Under arbitrary product measures, symmetric thresholds satisfy the strengthened inequality needed for read-once composition, uniformly in depth and fan-in. A joint description of each Fourier set refines the overlap estimate and recovers constant bounds for addressing. Exact selector identities extend the bound to orthogonal multiplexers with shared data. Rare activation preserves the optimal constant of unrestricted FEI. The proofs combine pivotal antichains, spectral reference measures, and product-measure composition.

entries.title: Robust Nonparametric Methods for $α$-Mixing Sequences via Median-of-Means
entries.abstract: The median-of-means (MoM) estimator is a robust alternative to the sample mean for heavy-tailed or contaminated data. While its non-asymptotic properties are well understood for i.i.d.\ samples, much less is known for dependent sequences. We establish non-asymptotic deviation bounds for the MoM estimator computed from consecutive blocks of an identically distributed $α$-mixing sequence, both for a single mean and uniformly over a class of functions (the median-of-means process). All bounds remain valid, with explicitly adjusted constants, when a sufficiently small fraction of the blocks is adversarially corrupted. As applications, we obtain deviation bounds for a median-of-means Nadaraya--Watson regression estimator, for the MoM kernel density estimator, and for empirical and Bahadur-type estimators of Value-at-Risk and Conditional Value-at-Risk. Finally, we show that the sampling of bulk materials, where the measurements form a spatially dependent random field, reduces to the one-dimensional setting if the samples are taken in well-separated groups.

entries.title: A Khintchine type inequality for non-independent random variables
entries.abstract: In this short note we give a Khintchine-type inequality involving non-independentrandom variables. The basic setting is inspired by Breuer-Major theorem and the proof is based on a hypercontractivity argument.

entries.title: Uniform-in-Time and Uniform-in-Temperature Particle Approximations of Coulomb MMD Flows
entries.abstract: We study particle approximations of maximum mean discrepancy (MMD) flows with the Coulomb kernel on the torus $\mathbb{T}^d$, $d\ge2$, driven by thermal noise of strength $τ\ge0$. For smooth, strictly positive initial and target densities and i.i.d. initial positions, we prove that the expected Wasserstein-1 distance between the empirical measure and the mean-field solution is at most of order $N^{-1/d}$ for $d\ge3$ and $\sqrt{(\log N)/N}$ for $d=2$, uniformly in time and in the temperature $τ\ge0$, including the deterministic case $τ=0$. At each fixed $τ>0$, we also prove propagation of chaos in total variation for any $k$-fold marginal distributions of particles, uniformly in time, with a bound of order $\sqrt{k/τ}$ times the empirical convergence rate. Our proof uses the modulated free-energy method of Bresch, Jabin, and Wang to reduce the particle convergence estimate to a relaxation estimate that controls the time integral of the mean-field velocity gradient uniformly in $τ\ge0$. Near zero temperature, where the smoothing effect of the noise degenerates, we obtain this estimate by recentering the dynamics at thermal equilibrium and using the damping generated by the Coulomb interaction.

entries.title: A clarification of Fermi's formula for the maximum of partial sums
entries.abstract: In Fermi's 1926 note, the expression assigned to the probability that all partial sums remain below a threshold is the complementary crossing probability. We obtain the correct probability from the same diffusion equation and locate the inconsistency in the final integration. We then state the limit for independent increments under the Lindeberg condition. A counterexample with smooth densities shows that small individual variances do not suffice to justify this limit. The probabilistic results are classical; the purpose of this note is to reconcile the stated event with the printed calculation and to make the sufficient hypotheses for the discrete limit explicit.

entries.title: Notes on Uniform Policy Score Bounds and Lipschitz Continuity for Truncated Gaussian, Product Cauchy, Boltzmann, and Softmax Policies
entries.abstract: We establish uniform score bounds and Lipschitz continuity for truncated Gaussian, Cauchy, Boltzmann, and softmax policies under explicitly stated parameterizations.

entries.title: FirstFit coloring process of random bipartite graphs and an online coloring lower bound in the random order model
entries.abstract: FirstFit colors each arriving vertex with the smallest positive integer absent from its previously colored neighborhood. We prove that this rule can require $n^{Ω(1)}$ many colors on certain bipartite graph of $n$ vertices even when the vertices arrive in a uniformly random order. This refutes the conjecture of Bosek, Gutowski, Lasoń, and Przybyło [BGLP24] that FirstFit uses a polylogarithmic expected number of colors on every bipartite graph in the random order model. We obtain the lower bound by analyzing the FirstFit coloring process on random bipartite graphs, where vertices arrive to either side with equal probability, and with an independent edge density $n^{-x}$ for some $0 < x < 1$. Our result can also be viewed as a qualitative strengthening of Kučera [Kuč91], who showed that, for every $ε> 0$, there are graphs with chromatic number at most $n^ε$ on which FirstFit uses $Ω(n/\log n)$ colors in expectation under a uniformly random order. Our result shows that such poor behavior of FirstFit already occurs for $χ(G) = 2$.

entries.title: A Berry--Esseen Bound of Order $(1+\log n)/\sqrt n$ for Peng's Central Limit Theorem
entries.abstract: We derive a quantitative central limit theorem under sublinear expectations from a spatial endpoint regularity estimate for the one-dimensional \(G\)-heat equation. For bounded Lipschitz initial data, the second spatial derivative and the time derivative of its solution are Lipschitz in space and \(1/2\)-Hölder in time away from the initial time. In particular, \([u_{xx}(t,\cdot)]_{\mathrm{Lip}}\le C_G\Lip(ϕ)/t\). Combining this estimate with the nonlinear Stein identity introduced in Song \cite{Song2020} and a replacement argument yields a bound of order \((1+\log n)/\sqrt n\) for bounded Lipschitz tests when the third absolute moment is finite and the lower variance is positive. The final replacement step is estimated directly, avoiding the nonintegrable singularity at time zero.

entries.title: Three Homoscedastic Gaussian Components Have at Most Four Modes
entries.abstract: Gaussian mixtures can have more modes than components. For three Gaussian components with a common covariance, four modes are attainable, whereas the best general upper bound was eight. We prove that four is the exact maximum in every dimension $d \ge 2$, for arbitrary means and positive weights. We further show that the sharp bound drops to three when the whitened means are collinear or form a right or obtuse triangle. The result covers degenerate modes without genericity or separate finiteness assumptions. Our proof maps modes to local minima of a separable free-energy functional on the probability simplex, reduces the problem to counting scalar inverse-function branches, and controls competing branches through curvature and stationary-height comparisons.

entries.title: Invariant Measures for Interacting Continuous-State Population Models
entries.abstract: We study invariant probabilities for nonlinear two-population branching systems with competition, cooperation, or predator--prey interaction, driven by Brownian noise and spectrally positive stable jumps. Without immigration, every invariant probability of a conservative competitive or predator--prey system is concentrated on the boundary under either boundary convention. With nontrivial axis dynamics, coordinatewise continuation admits only the point mass at the origin. For cooperative systems, we give criteria for boundary concentration and interior stationarity, including a sharp criterion for bilinear cooperation with a common relative noise exponent. With immigration, explicit parameter conditions yield existence and stationary moment bounds. For square-root diffusions with positive immigration, these conditions ensure interior concentration and full support on the closed quadrant. Further lower bounds on immigration rates give uniqueness and convergence of time-averaged transition laws.

entries.title: Explicit descriptions of all 1-Meixner random vectors
entries.abstract: The 1-Meixner random vectors consist of $d$ real-valued random variables, having finite moments of all orders, for which the commutators between their joint semi-quantum operators and the multiplication operators that they generate are linear combinations of these multiplication operators and the identity operator. This property of random variables imposes a system of first-order partial differential equations on their joint Laplace transform on a neighborhood of $0$ in a Euclidean $d$-space. We provide explicit descriptions of all solutions of the system just mentioned in every dimension $d$.

entries.title: Fuglede--Kadison Determinants of Shifted Matrix Semicircles
entries.abstract: We prove a variational formula for the Fuglede-Kadison determinant of a self-adjoint matrix semicircle $S_a = a \otimes 1 + \sum_j A_j \otimes s_j$ with deterministic mean $a$. For every real $z$, $\log Δ(S_a - z) = -1/2 + \inf_b F_z(b)$, where the infimum is over positive definite matrices $b$ such that the map $X \mapsto bXb - \sum_j A_j X A_j$ is positive semidefinite, and $F_z$ is an explicit geodesically convex function. Both sides equal $-\infty$ exactly when $z$ is an atom of the spectral measure. The formula was proposed, without proof, in a recent post of Speicher. In the centered case $a=0$ it gives a new proof of the Mai-Speicher capacity formula, and by hermitization it yields a finite-dimensional variational formula for the logarithmic potential of the Brown measure of an arbitrary matrix-valued semicircular element. The proof identifies the determinant with the value of the Dyson action at its critical point and rewrites this critical-point problem as a saddle problem in three matrix variables. For a spectral parameter $z + i\varepsilon$ in the upper half-plane, eliminating two of the variables gives a geodesically convex minimization whose global minimizer is the positive factor $b_\varepsilon$ in a symmetric unitary factorization of the matrix Cauchy transform. The formula on the real axis follows by letting $\varepsilon \to 0$ in the optimal values, with no compactness assumption on the minimizers. At points where the boundary value of the Cauchy transform is nondegenerate, the scales $b_\varepsilon$ converge and the infimum is attained at their limit; this minimizer lies on the boundary of the feasible set when $z$ is in the support of the spectral measure and in its interior when $z$ is in the resolvent set.

entries.title: Closed forms all the way up: the sample variance of four observations
entries.abstract: The distribution function $F(y)=\Pr(S^2\le y)$ of the sample variance $S^2$ of four independent observations is elementary on its entire support for every polynomial parent density on $[0,1]$ (without loss of generality), and we give it in finite closed form for the uniform, Beta$(2,1)$ and Beta$(2,2)$ parents. The support splits at $y = 1/6$, $2/9$ and $1/4$, with the ceiling at $1/3$, all fixed by geometry: in coordinates aligned with the cube diagonal the event $S^2\le y$ is a ball of radius $\sqrt{3y}$, the cube projects to a rhombic dodecahedron, and these are the levels at which the ball reaches its faces, edges and two kinds of vertices. The divergence theorem reduces every moment of the clipped ball to integrals along circular arcs, so each regime closes in algebraic functions of $\sqrt{y}$ and inverse trigonometric functions. For the uniform parent the only non-obvious constant is $K_g = 12\sqrt2\arctan\sqrt2$, proportional to the mean width of the cuboctahedron; the Beta constants are rational expressions in $π$, $\sqrt2$, $\sqrt3$ and $\arctan\sqrt2$, as in the uniform case. At $n = 4$ the normal-theory $χ^2$ recipe used in acceptance testing misplaces the $99$th percentile of $S^2$ by $50\%$ for the uniform parent. For three observations, polynomial parents also give elementary closed forms (arXiv:2609.25333), but two elementary cases in a row do not guarantee a third, and we make no claim beyond $n = 4$.

entries.title: Weak universality of global dynamics for the fractional hyperbolic $Φ^4_3$-model
entries.abstract: We continue the study of weak universality for the fractional hyperbolic $Φ^4_3$-model initiated by Tzvetkov, Wang, and the author (2023). In this work, we establish weak universality in a regime where the associated Gibbs measure is mutually singular with respect to the underlying Gaussian measure. We first investigate the weak convergence of the Gibbs measures associated with macroscopic models to the fractional $Φ^4_3$-measure constructed by Tzvetkov, Wang, and the author (2023). We then obtain a structured representation for these Gibbs measures via the stochastic quantization method. Finally, we prove dynamical weak universality for the fractional hyperbolic $Φ^4_3$-model by using an extended second order expansion and exploiting the invariance of the Gibbs measures.

entries.title: Double-arc rearrangement and the symmetric isoperimetric problem in Gauss space
entries.abstract: We provide a new rearrangement in Gauss space transforming symmetric sets while decreasing their Gaussian perimeter. We use this rearrangement to analyze the minimizers of the Gaussian perimeter among symmetric sets.

entries.title: Duality Theory for Filter Stability in Hidden Markov Models
entries.abstract: This article is concerned with the problem of nonlinear (stochastic) filter stability for a discrete time hidden Markov model (HMM) with finite state and observation spaces. For this purpose, a comprehensive duality theory is developed whereby the dual control system is a backward stochastic difference equation (BSDE). The duality is expressed in two inter-related forms. In its variational form, the minimum mean squared error of optimal filtering equals the value of a dual optimal control problem. In its structural form, controllability (resp. stabilizability) of the BSDE and observability (resp. detectability) of the HMM are dual properties. The dual optimal control problem supplies the Lyapunov function and the dissipation: the former is the value function (a variance), the latter the optimal running cost accumulated over the horizon. The main result is an invariance principle: under any one of three model properties---ergodicity of the Markov matrix, or observability or detectability of the HMM---zero dissipation over a finite horizon forces the Lyapunov function to vanish. A converse is also obtained: detectability is necessary. Two applications are given. The first is filter stability in chi-squared divergence: the invariance principle is applied in the manner of LaSalle, to limits of trajectories along which the dissipation vanishes asymptotically, the role of the model properties being to render the zero-dissipation set trivial. The second is a quantitative form of the invariance principle, through a Poincare constant, from which convergence rates follow. Both the model properties that govern stability and the Lyapunov function that certifies it are thus obtained from a dual optimal control problem, as in the classical theory for the linear Gaussian model.

entries.title: An Exact Hausdorff Measure as Natural Length for SLE
entries.abstract: Fix $0<κ<8$ and put $d=1+κ/8$. Recent work by OpenAI identifies an explicit exact Hausdorff gauge \( h_κ(r)=r^d\bigl(\log\log(1/r)\bigr)^{(2-d)/2} \) for sufficiently small $r$ for chordal $\mathrm{SLE}_κ$: the corresponding Hausdorff measure is almost surely positive and finite on every segment $γ([s,t])$ with $0<s<t<\infty$, and has finite expectation in bounded subsets of the plane. We show that this Hausdorff measure is a deterministic positive constant multiple of the occupation measure (natural length) constructed by Lawler and Rezaei.

entries.title: Non-uniqueness for McKean--Vlasov SDEs with Hölder diffusion coefficients
entries.abstract: We show that uniqueness may fail for one-dimensional McKean--Vlasov stochastic differential equations with Hölder continuous diffusion coefficients. More precisely, for every \(α\in(1/2,1)\), we construct an equation with a diffusion coefficient that is \(α\)-Hölder continuous in the state variable, Lipschitz continuous in the measure variable, and of linear growth, for which uniqueness in law and pathwise uniqueness fail. The construction relies on a spreading estimate together with a Schauder fixed-point argument.

entries.title: DisCo Algebra: Why Disintegration and Combination Are Not Inverses
entries.abstract: We present DisCo algebra---a compositional framework for joint probability built from a symmetric cooperad (disintegration) and a symmetric operad (combination) on the bare family $\mathcal{P}_n=\mathrm{Prob}([0,1]^n)$. No probability integral transform, no external summary functions, no enrichment of objects with conditional kernels. The disintegration side uses block-wise joint CDFs as intrinsic, measure-determined 1D summaries, yielding a lossy compression. The combination side reads the same summaries and reconstructs via regular conditional measures, yielding a lossless embedding. We prove that combination followed by disintegration is the identity on admissible inputs, but disintegration followed by combination is not---the information loss is exactly the conditional KL divergence between the true conditional distribution and the conditionally independent product. This asymmetry reveals a hard limit on how much cross-block dependence can be captured by scalar block summaries.

entries.title: Overlap distributions under the Gibbs measure of a Haar model of $\log|ζ|$ on and near the critical line
entries.abstract: We study the Gibbs measure of $H(h) = \Re\sum_{p^{j} \leq X}U_{p}^{j}/(j p^{j(σ+ i h)})$, a random field modeling large values of the log-modulus of the Riemann zeta function on and near the critical line, where the $U_{p}$ are independent and uniformly distributed on the complex unit circle. Writing $t = \log \log T$, the cutoff $X$ and real part $σ$ may vary with $T$ subject to $T^{1/t^Φ} \leq X \leq T^{1/t^ϕ}$ and $0 \leq σ- 1/2 \leq C_σt^Φ/\log T$, for fixed $Φ\geq ϕ> 1/2$ and $C_σ > 0$. On $I_θ = [ - (\log T)^θ,(\log T)^θ]$, define the Gibbs measure $G_{β,σ,T}^{\mathrm{H}}(\mathrm{d}h) := e^{βH(h)}\mathrm{d}h/\int_{I_θ}e^{βH(h')}\mathrm{d}h'$. For every fixed $θ> - 1$ and inverse temperature $β> 0$, the limiting joint distributions of correlations (overlaps) among points sampled from this measure are determined after averaging over the Haar phases. At and below $β_{c}(θ) = 2\sqrt{1 + (θ\vee 0)}$, the limiting two-overlap distribution is concentrated at $q_{0} = |θ\wedge 0|$. Above this threshold, it assigns masses $β_{c}(θ)/β$ and $1 - β_{c}(θ)/β$ to $q_{0}$ and $1$, respectively, and the limiting joint overlap distribution is described by a Poisson-Dirichlet process of parameter $β_{c}(θ)/β$. Approximate Ghirlanda-Guerra identities are shown to hold uniformly for bounded deterministic functions of the sampled positions. This paper is the first in a series devoted to extending these results to $\log|ζ|$ near the critical line.

entries.title: From Cauchy to Gaussian: Sharp Lower Deviations and Ehrhard-Type Inequality
entries.abstract: We establish dimension-free, pointwise optimal lower-deviation bounds for convex functions under spherically symmetric Cauchy-type measures. These bounds use either mean-variance normalization or moments about the median, the latter covering the Cauchy case where the mean and variance are unavailable. By approximation with a parametrized family the Cauchy-type measures, our results recover the Gaussian setting of Paouris and Valettas \cite{PaourisValettas18} and strengthen their variance-sensitive estimate to a sharp bound, with a complete equality characterization. This goes beyond the partial improvements obtained in subsequent work. We also prove an Ehrhard-type inequality for arbitrary convex sets under these Cauchy-type measures in every dimension and characterize all equality cases. This resolves a conjecture posed by Byczkowski, Małecki and Żak \cite{ByczkowskiMaleckiZak22}. The proof follows from a variational argument combined with the joint concavity of fiber rearrangement. The geometric inequality reduces distributions of convex observables to one-dimensional convex transforms, yielding the sharp lower-deviation bounds.

entries.title: Multi-type $Λ$-Wright--Fisher processes with polynomial drift: Bernstein duality, long-term behaviour, and simulation of moments
